Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted. Isaiah 53:3-4 (KJV) He wept at a grave. He was betrayed by a friend who ate his bread. In the garden he asked for the cup to pass. On the cross he cried out that God had forsaken him, so that those who trust him will never be forsaken (Matthew 27:46, Hebrews 13:5). On the third day he rose, and he lives now. The Larger Catechism says the Son became man so that he might have a fellow feeling of our infirmities, and so that we might have comfort and access with boldness unto the throne of grace (Q&A 39). For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need. Hebrews 4:15-16 (KJV) This is your time of need. Come.

title: Grief and Hard Times
text: Prayer When You Cannot Pray Grief can take the words out of your mouth. God has made provision for that too. Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. Romans 8:26 (KJV) If you belong to Christ, a groan with no words in it can be a prayer. The Spirit himself carries it. And if you are his, the Son is praying for you at the right hand of God, as he prayed for Peter before Peter ever fell (Romans 8:34, Luke 22:32). When you have no words, borrow the prayers God gave his people. Read Psalm 13 aloud, or Psalm 42, or Psalm 88. Psalm 88 ends in the dark, yet its first words call God the God of my salvation. David asked God to put his tears into his bottle (Psalm 56:8). God has no bottle and needs none. The picture means that he keeps count of every tear, and not one is lost.

title: Grief and Hard Times
text: The church Do Not Carry It Alone This page can hand you Scripture. It cannot sit with you, pray over you, or bring you a meal. Christ gave those things to his church. Call your pastor or an elder today. If one of them is the one hurting you, call another pastor you trust. You do not have to explain it well. Say that something has happened and ask him to pray with you. If the need is money or meals or rides, tell your deacons. That is what the office is for. Peter told the elders, Feed the flock of God which is among you, taking the oversight thereof (1 Peter 5:2). Letting them do it is not a burden you lay on them. It is the work Christ gave them. When an elder comes, ask when he will come again. Go to worship on the Lord’s Day, even if you only sit and weep. Sit under the Word, and pray with God’s people. If you are a communing member, come to the Lord’s Table. It was given for the relief of weak and doubting Christians too (Larger Catechism Q&A 172). The Word, the sacraments, and prayer are the means by which Christ gives his people the benefits of his redemption (Shorter Catechism Q&A 88), and by them weak faith is strengthened (Westminster Confession 14.1). Yours may be weak this week. Where you can, put off large decisions for a while, and do not make any of them alone. Getting safe is never a decision to put off. If you have no church, find a faithful one near you and go this Sunday. Look for one where Christ is preached from the whole Bible, where baptism and the Lord’s Supper are given as he commanded, and where elders watch over the flock. Then ask how to join it. Christ never meant for one of his sheep to walk alone. If you do not know where to start, write to me . I keep this site. I am not a pastor, and I cannot always answer quickly. In an emergency, do not wait on me. Call 911 , or call 988 or text 988 . But I will pray for you, and I will help you look for a church. Blessed be God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort; Who comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God. 2 Corinthians 1:3-4 (KJV) One day you may sit with someone else in this same dark. The comfort God gives you now is meant to be passed on.

title: Grief and Hard Times
text: If you do not know him Believest Thou This Maybe you came here because of a death, a diagnosis, a broken home, or a lost job, and you are not a Christian. The promises here belong to those who belong to Christ. They can be yours. Jesus spoke these words to a grieving woman on the road outside her village, four days after her brother was buried (John 11:17, 20). Then he asked her a question. He asks you the same one. Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die. Believest thou this? John 11:25-26 (KJV) If you came here grieving someone, this is not a word about them. Leave them with God. It is a word about you. Death came into the world through sin, and one day you will stand before God yourself (Romans 5:12, Hebrews 9:27). But Christ died in the place of sinners and bore the punishment their sins deserved, and on the third day he rose again. Everyone who turns from sin and trusts him alone is forgiven and counted righteous for his sake (Shorter Catechism Q&A 33, 87). He said that whoever comes to him he will in no wise cast out (John 6:37). Call on him tonight, in your own words. Whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved (Romans 10:13). Do not wait until the grief lifts. Come as you are, with the grief. The gospel page sets it out in full. Read it slowly.

title: When Someone You Love Has Died
text: The house is quiet, or it is full of people, and either way the one you want is not in it. You do not have to be strong tonight. Christ has stood where you are standing.

title: When Someone You Love Has Died
section: When you are ready to search your heart
text: When you are ready to search your heart Not tonight. This is not a search for some sin behind their death. God has not told you why, and no one may guess (Deuteronomy 29:29). Your grief is not sin. Jesus wept. But other things can creep in beside grief, and it is a mercy to see them early. Pray, Search me, O God, and know my heart (Psalm 139:23). You may pour out all your sorrow to God, and even ask him why. Jesus did, on the cross. But do not accuse him. Job lost his children in one day, and in all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly (Job 1:22). Watch for bitterness toward family or friends (Ephesians 4:31). Watch for drink or drugs to dull the nights. Do not stay away from worship for long. And do not let love for the one you lost take the place of God. Loving them is not the sin. Living for them in place of him would be. If you find any of this in you, do not despair. Thomas was not with the others the first time the risen Jesus came. Eight days later he was back with them, and Jesus came again and said, Peace be unto you (John 20:24-26). Christ died for sins like these, and rose again, and he turns away no one who comes to him. Confess it, and he is faithful and just to forgive (1 John 1:9). If you do not know Christ, or are not sure you do, his own question is below .

title: When Your Husband or Wife Has Died
text: The one who knew you best is gone, and half of every habit in the house went with them. There is no timetable for this. Christ saw to those left behind even while he was dying.

title: When Your Husband or Wife Has Died
section: When you are ready to ask about heaven
text: When you are ready to ask about heaven If your husband or wife belonged to Christ, their soul is with him now, made perfect in holiness (Shorter Catechism Q&A 37). At the resurrection, believers being raised up in glory, shall be openly acknowledged and acquitted in the day of judgment, and made perfectly blessed in the full enjoying of God to all eternity. Westminster Shorter Catechism Q&A 38 Paul says that when the Lord comes, the dead in Christ shall rise first. Then his people who are still alive will be caught up together with them, and so shall we ever be with the Lord (1 Thessalonians 4:16-17). In the resurrection, Jesus said, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven (Matthew 22:30). Yet Christ’s people are raised as themselves, with bodies made like his glorious body (Philippians 3:21). Marriage is God’s gift for this life (Romans 7:2). Scripture says less than we might wish about how his people will know one another there. But the one who gave his mother a home from the cross is there now, and he is their joy. If you are his, you will see him on the day he chooses, not the day you choose. Until then, he has not finished with your life here.

title: When Your Husband or Wife Has Died
section: When you are ready to search your heart
text: When you are ready to search your heart Your grief is not sin. Missing them is not sin, however long it lasts. This is not a search for some sin behind their death. God has not told you why, and no one may guess (Deuteronomy 29:29). But a long sorrow opens doors. Ask God to search you (Psalm 139:23). Naomi buried her husband and both her sons. She said, Call me not Naomi, call me Mara (Ruth 1:20). Mara means bitter. You may tell God it is bitter. Do not let it take root against him or his people. Loneliness can keep you home from worship. It can send you to drink to fill the evenings, or rush you toward someone new before you have grieved and sought counsel. And the one you lost can come to fill the place only God should fill. God did not scold Naomi, and he did not leave her alone. From her house came King David, and at last Christ (Ruth 4:14-17, Matthew 1:5-6). He has not promised you her ending. He offers you her Redeemer. Like Anna, keep close to God’s house and to prayer (Luke 2:37). If you find any of this in you, bring it to Christ. He died for sins like these and rose again, and he turns away no one who comes to him. Confess it, and he is faithful and just to forgive (1 John 1:9). If you do not know Christ, or are not sure you do, his own question is below .

title: When Your Child Has Died
text: No parent should outlive a child, and every part of you knows it. Whether you lost a baby you barely held, or never held at all, or a son or daughter you raised, Christ has not looked away.

title: When Your Child Has Died
section: If you lost a baby or a little child
text: If you lost a baby or a little child People brought young children to Jesus, some of them infants (Luke 18:15). When his disciples rebuked those who brought them, Jesus was much displeased, and said, Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not (Mark 10:13-14). Suffer here means allow. And he took them up in his arms, put his hands upon them, and blessed them. Mark 10:16 (KJV) That is his heart toward little ones. Those hands were later nailed to a cross for sinners, and on the third day he rose (John 20:25). His heart has not changed. David said to God, Thou hast covered me in my mother’s womb (Psalm 139:13). Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in thy book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them. Psalm 139:16 (KJV) Unperfect is the old word for not yet formed, not a word for flawed. God saw your child before your child was fully made. The book is a picture of God’s knowledge and his plan, and what it pictures is real. He knew your child. However early the loss came, you lost a child. When King David’s baby son died, David rose from the ground and worshipped (2 Samuel 12:20). Then he told his servants why. And he said, While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept: for I said, Who can tell whether God will be gracious to me, that the child may live? But now he is dead, wherefore should I fast? can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me. 2 Samuel 12:22-23 (KJV) David stopped fasting because the time for asking was over. The time for grief was not over. He spoke of his son with hope, and then he went on living. He ate that same day, and he comforted his wife (2 Samuel 12:20, 24). You may weep for your little one. Earlier in that chapter the prophet Nathan told David that this child would die because of David’s sin. In the same breath he told him, The Lord also hath put away thy sin (2 Samuel 12:13-14). No prophet has told you that your child died for your sin, and God has not said it. Without a word from God, no one may trace a sorrow to a particular sin (John 9:3, Deuteronomy 29:29). Many mothers blame their own bodies. A body that could not carry a child is not a sin. If you are in Christ, there is no condemnation for you (Romans 8:1), and your baby’s death is not a sentence on you. For a believer even a Father’s chastening is never payment for sin, because Christ paid it all. A little one cannot understand a sermon or put faith into words. That is no barrier to the Spirit of Christ, who works when, and where, and how he pleases (Westminster Confession 10.3). Grace does not wait for anyone to be old enough. The Canons of Dort, a sister Reformed confession, teach that believing parents need not doubt the salvation of the children God takes in infancy. They rest this on God’s Word, which calls the children of believers holy (1 Corinthians 7:14), not by nature but by his covenant of grace (Canons of Dort 1.17). That hope rests on God’s promise, not on how well you lived. Whatever you do not know tonight, you may leave your child with the Judge of all the earth, who will do right (Genesis 18:25). If your baby died before birth, the next part is for you. If not, go on to the part for every grieving parent .

title: When Your Child Has Died
section: If your baby died before birth
text: If your baby died before birth A miscarriage or a stillbirth is the death of a child. Some people around you may not see it that way. They may say nothing at all, or say it was for the best, or that you can try again. They usually mean well, but a child is not replaced by another child. Scripture counts the little one you carried as a person, known by God and made in his image (Jeremiah 1:5, Luke 1:41). You are not making too much of this. You lost a son or a daughter. Many mothers search their memories for what they did wrong. Doctors find that most early losses come from causes no mother could have caused or stopped. And even where you wonder, God has not laid this at your feet. He knoweth our frame (Psalm 103:14). Fathers grieve this too, though often more quietly and later. A father may feel he has to be strong for his wife and so never mourn at all. Husbands, weep with your wives, and let your church care for you both. If the loss came early, there may be nothing to bury, and no one outside your home may have known. That can make the grief lonelier. You may still mark it. Give your baby a name, tell your pastor, and pray together as a family. Due dates and the day of the loss may be hard for years, and that is not a weakness of faith. If you are afraid to hope for another child, or if another child never comes, bring that fear to the God who gives and takes away (Job 1:21). He is not cruel, and he is not careless with you. If in the past you chose to end a pregnancy, you may grieve that child too. A doctor’s care after your baby had already died is not that choice. For that choice there is full pardon in Christ, for all who come to him. Read If You Have Had an Abortion and What I did is too great to forgive . The next part is for parents of an older child. The part for every grieving parent is for you too.

title: When Your Child Has Died
section: If your son or daughter was older
text: If your son or daughter was older Jesus once met a funeral at the gate of a town called Nain. The dead man was the only son of his mother, and she was a widow (Luke 7:12). And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not. And he came and touched the bier: and they that bare him stood still. And he said, Young man, I say unto thee, Arise. And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he delivered him to his mother. Luke 7:13-15 (KJV) A bier was the open frame the dead were carried on. Jesus had compassion on her before she asked him for anything. He could tell her not to weep, because he was about to give her son back. He was not rebuking her tears, or yours. He did not raise every dead son or daughter in Israel. The widow’s son at Nain, and the girl of twelve he took by the hand (Mark 5:41-42), were signs pointing ahead to the last day, when he will call his people out of their graves. They were not promises for today. When a great wind brought a house down on Job’s children, Job tore his robe, fell down on the ground, and worshipped. In all this Job sinned not (Job 1:18-22). Grief and worship stand on the same ground. If your son or daughter trusted Christ, no man can pluck them out of his hand (John 10:28-29). Death could not do it either (Romans 8:38-39). The souls of believers are at their death made perfect in holiness, and do immediately pass into glory; and their bodies, being still united to Christ, do rest in their graves till the resurrection. Westminster Shorter Catechism Q&A 37 If they are his, they are with him now, and every sin they ever fought is gone. If you do not know where your child stood with God, that is too heavy to carry alone tonight. You are not asked to settle where they are. Leave them with the Judge of all the earth, who will do right (Genesis 18:25), and bring your own soul to Christ. Read When You Fear They Did Not Know Christ , and tell your pastor this week. If your son or daughter took their own life, that sorrow has its own place here . If someone else took your child’s life, by carelessness or by violence, your anger at that wrong is not sin in itself. Scripture says, Be ye angry, and sin not (Ephesians 4:26). God says, Vengeance is mine, and he promises to repay (Romans 12:19). He gave the ruler the sword for this very wrong (Romans 13:4), so pressing for justice in the courts is not revenge.

title: When Your Child Has Died
text: For every grieving parent Many parents replay every moment, what they ate or lifted, the last night, the keys they handed over, the sign they missed. Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him. For he knoweth our frame; he remembereth that we are dust. Psalm 103:13-14 (KJV) You could not see what only God could see. Moses told God’s people that underneath are the everlasting arms (Deuteronomy 33:27). Those arms are a picture, since God is a Spirit, and the care they picture is real. But the Son of God took a real body, with real arms. He took up little children in those arms and blessed them. Then he died for sinners, and on the third day he rose. Now he says he was dead and is alive for evermore, and holds the keys of death (Revelation 1:18). Keys picture his authority over death, and that authority is real. He will lose none of those the Father has given him, and he will raise them up at the last day (John 6:39). Before you sleep, do these three things. If your child died long ago and the grief has not let go, that is not a failure of faith, and these are for you too. Pour out your heart to God. He is a refuge for us (Psalm 62:8). Tell him all of it tonight. You do not need fine words. Call your pastor or an elder. Even at night. Let him help you with a burial or a service if you want one, even for a baby lost early. You may give your baby a name. If you have no church, call a Christian friend, and read Do Not Carry It Alone below. Eat a little, and rest. Lie down even if sleep will not come. If you are married, be patient with each other. Husbands and wives grieve differently, and fathers often grieve later and more quietly. If you have other children, keep them close. They grieve too. If your body is healing from this loss, rest, and call your doctor if the bleeding is heavy or you have a fever. If you find yourself wanting to follow your child, call 988 or text 988 tonight, and tell someone near you.

title: When Your Child Has Died
section: When you are ready to search your heart
text: When you are ready to search your heart Not tonight. This is not the replaying of every moment, and it is not a search for some sin behind your child’s death. God has not told you why, and no one may guess (Deuteronomy 29:29). Your grief is not sin. But this sorrow can open doors. Ask God to search you (Psalm 139:23). Anger at God may come. Tell him, but do not charge him with wrong. Job lost all his children, and he did not charge God foolishly (Job 1:22). Grief can turn a husband and wife against each other, so that each blames the other or shuts the other out. If anyone at home hurt your child or is hurting you, get safe first . Otherwise, turn toward each other, forgiving one another (Ephesians 4:32). Other people’s children may be painful to see. That ache is not sin, but it can grow into envy and bitterness. If you have other children, sorrow can make it hard to give them what they need. Let others help you care for them. If a heaviness will not lift, that may be an illness and not a sin. See a doctor, and read When You Are Depressed . If you find any of this in you, do not despair. Christ died for sins like these, and rose again, and he turns away no one who comes to him. Confess it, and he is faithful and just to forgive (1 John 1:9). If you do not know Christ, or are not sure you do, his own question is below .

title: When You Fear They Did Not Know Christ
text: Some of us bury people we love without knowing whether they knew Christ. Some of you are not unsure. You fear you know. This is for you too, and you are not asked to settle anything tonight.

title: When You Fear They Did Not Know Christ
section: When you are ready to search your heart
text: When you are ready to search your heart Paul says, Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith (2 Corinthians 13:5). Do not look for the answer in how strong your faith feels. Look to Christ. If you are his and this fear has shaken you, read Am I Really Saved? This fear brings temptations of its own. One is to turn from God for their sake, as if staying away from Christ could help the one you lost. It cannot, and coming to him does not betray them. Another is to think the Judge is hard. He is the one who wept over Jerusalem. Another is to keep accusing yourself for what you did not say. Bring that to Christ too. In him, whatever was truly sin is forgiven, and whatever was never in your hands you may lay down. Christ died on the cross for sinners and rose again, and he turns away no one who comes. Scripture still says, whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely (Revelation 22:17). Come, and keep to the means he gave, his Word, prayer, and the Lord’s Day with his people.

title: When Someone You Love Took Their Own Life
text: A death like this leaves questions no other death leaves. You may be carrying grief and guilt and fear all at once. God saw what you could not see, and he is near you now.

title: When Someone You Love Took Their Own Life
section: When you are ready to search your heart
text: When you are ready to search your heart Not tonight. In the weeks ahead, ask God to search you (Psalm 139:23), and to sort what is truly yours from what is not. Much of what you carry may be false guilt. You did not choose this for them. If you truly sinned against them, confess it plainly, and in Christ it is forgiven (1 John 1:9). Even then, the choice was not yours. What was never yours, you may lay down. Anger may come too, at the one who died, or at people you think should have seen it. Be ye angry, and sin not (Ephesians 4:26). Do not let it settle into bitterness. If it rises against God, tell him so, but do not let it harden into a charge that he has done wrong. Shame may tell you to stay away from church. Go anyway. This death is not your disgrace. If the thought of following them comes, stop the searching and get help tonight. You are not strange, and you must not carry it alone. Call 988 or text 988 , and tell someone near you. Christ died on the cross for sinners and rose again. Whoever you are, come to him with what is truly yours, and leave the rest with him. If you do not know Christ, or are not sure you do, his own question is below .

title: When Serious Illness Comes
text: One conversation in a small room, and the future looks different than it did this morning, for you or for someone you love. Or it has looked this way for years. You do not have to be brave tonight. Your times are in God’s hand.

title: When Serious Illness Comes
section: When it has gone on for years
text: When it has gone on for years You have asked for healing more times than you can count, and fewer people ask how you are. God put this prayer in the Bible for you. How long wilt thou forget me, O Lord ? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me? How long shall I take counsel in my soul, having sorrow in my heart daily? how long shall mine enemy be exalted over me? Psalm 13:1-2 (KJV) David felt forgotten, and he said so. A hidden face is a picture of a season when God’s favor cannot be felt, and such seasons are real (WCF 18.4). But God had not forgotten David, and by the end of the psalm David trusts his mercy again (13:5). For you it may take longer than six verses. He got there by praying the question, not by hiding it. If you are his, the grace Paul was given is yours too. It does not always take the weakness away. It holds you up inside it. Your outward man, the body, may be wasting away. Yet the inward man is renewed day by day (2 Corinthians 4:16). Paul also says the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us (Romans 8:18). That does not make your pain small. It makes the glory great. You may keep asking, and you may rest from asking. Let others pray when you cannot. And tell your elders you are still here, since churches forget the long sick. If the long years bring thoughts of ending your life, tell someone near you, and call 988 or text 988 . God has not finished with your life.

title: When Serious Illness Comes
section: If you are caring for someone
text: If you are caring for someone Maybe it is a hospital room, or hospice, or the long decline of a parent, a husband or wife, or a child. You are tired in ways few people see. When Lazarus was sick, his sisters sent Jesus this word, Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest is sick (John 11:3). Pray that with their name in it. God told his people, even to hoar hairs will I carry you (Isaiah 46:4). Hoar hairs are gray hairs. The carrying is a picture of his keeping, and his keeping is real. If they are his, he will carry them all the way, and if you are his, he carries you too. Caring for them is Christlike work. While he was dying, Jesus saw to his mother’s care (John 19:26-27). Accept help, and give people real jobs, for we are told to bear one another’s burdens (Galatians 6:2). Choosing a care home is not a failure of love. God works through means, and good nurses are among them. If dementia is taking their memory, they may no longer know your name. That is a real grief, a goodbye that comes a little at a time, and you may mourn it. They may forget the Lord’s name too. If they are his, he will not forget them (Isaiah 49:15). Will God Keep Me to the End? says more.

title: When Serious Illness Comes
text: If death is near For those who belong to Christ, death does not take them from him. It brings them to him. Jesus told the dying thief beside him, who had asked only to be remembered, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise (Luke 23:42-43). At death the souls of believers are made perfect in holiness and immediately pass into glory, and their bodies, still united to Christ, rest in their graves till the resurrection (Shorter Catechism Q&A 37). Christ rose, and they will rise. Paul called being with Christ far better, yet said his staying was more needful for others (Philippians 1:23-24). While God keeps you here, your days are not wasted. Jesus told his disciples not to let their hearts be troubled. He has gone to prepare a place for his people, and when he comes again he will receive them to himself, that where he is, they may be also (John 14:1-3). You may face hard choices about treatment, for yourself or for someone who can no longer speak. The Larger Catechism forbids the neglecting or withdrawing the lawful and necessary means of preservation of life (Q&A 136). A treatment that can no longer preserve life, and would only lengthen dying, is not such a means. You may say no to it, or stop it, and that is not giving up on God. But no one may end the life God gave, by a prescription or in any other way. Talk these choices over with your elders and your doctors. If you fear pain, ask about hospice care, which is there to ease it. If you fear being a burden, let those who love you carry you. If pain or fear is pushing you toward ending your life, tell someone near you, and call 988 or text 988 . Tell your family where your hope is, and call for your elders to pray with you (James 5:14). If you dread dying itself, read Afraid of Dying . If you are keeping watch at the bed, you do not need many words. Hold their hand, read Psalm 23 aloud, and pray. If you do not know where they stand with God, it is not too late to pray for them, to speak of Christ simply, or to ask your pastor to come.

title: When Serious Illness Comes
section: When you are ready to search your heart
text: When you are ready to search your heart This is not a search for why you are sick. When his disciples asked whose sin had made a man blind, Jesus turned them from that question to the works of God (John 9:2-3). It is a look at how you are bearing it. You may lament. David said, I poured out my complaint before him (Psalm 142:2). Lament takes the complaint to God. Murmuring turns it against him, as if he had wronged you. The Larger Catechism counts patient bearing of the hand of God among the duties of the sixth commandment (Q&A 135). There is a quieter sin too, trusting the doctors and forgetting the Lord. Go to the doctor, and pray, My help cometh from the Lord , which made heaven and earth (Psalm 121:2). Long pain can make us sharp with the ones who care for us, and a caregiver may find resentment growing in the long nights. Needing care is not the sin, and it does not make you a burden they would be better without. If you find these in you, bring them to Christ. He never murmured against his Father, and he went to the cross for murmuring sinners. He rose, and he turns away no one who comes. Confess it, and he is faithful and just to forgive (1 John 1:9). Then ask him for grace for this one day. If you do not know Christ, or are not sure you do, his own question is below .

title: When Your Marriage Is Breaking
text: You were left, or betrayed, or handed papers you did not want. The one who promised to stay did not. Whether you are the husband or the wife, Christ knows what it is to be betrayed.

title: When Your Marriage Is Breaking
section: What God has said about divorce
text: What God has said about divorce If you are afraid at home, getting safe comes first , and all of this can wait. Leaving to be safe is not divorce, and it needs none of the grounds below. Someone may have told you that God hates divorce, as if it were a word against you. In Malachi God says he hateth putting away, and in the same breath he condemns violence. He was rebuking husbands who dealt treacherously against the wife of their youth (Malachi 2:14-16). It is a word against the one who breaks faith, not the one who was put away or left. Jesus named one ground for divorce, fornication (Matthew 19:9). Paul speaks of a believer whose unbelieving spouse departs, and says God hath called us to peace (1 Corinthians 7:15). The Confession sums these up. It names only two grounds for divorce. One is adultery. The other is willful desertion that neither the church nor the government can remedy (WCF 24.5, 24.6). It protects the innocent party. It calls for a public and orderly course, so no one judges his own case. That is a mercy. You do not have to decide this alone, and this page will not decide it for you. Your elders can guide you. If a door is still open and it is safe, pray for repentance, and with your elders’ help seek reconciliation, as much as lieth in you (Romans 12:18). If no one is hurting you, but you are worn out and want out, that weariness is real. Tell God all of it. Then go to your elders before you take any step toward divorce (1 Corinthians 7:10-11). The heart is quick to find reasons, without just cause, to put asunder what God has joined (Matthew 19:6, WCF 24.6).

title: When Your Marriage Is Breaking
section: When you are ready to search your heart
text: When you are ready to search your heart Not tonight. This is not a search for your share of the blame. Adultery and desertion are the sin of the one who does them, and violence is never the fault of the one who is hurt. But any heart can sin in how it bears a wrong, and it is a mercy to see it. Anger at a real wrong is not sin in itself (Ephesians 4:26). But a wound can grow into bitterness, a grudge that keeps growing out of sight. Paul says to put away all bitterness, and to be tenderhearted, forgiving one another (Ephesians 4:31-32). Forgiving does not mean saying it was small, trusting someone who has not proved safe, going back into danger, or giving up on justice. It means giving up revenge and leaving the debt with God. Loneliness can also look for comfort in another person, in pornography , or in drink . Do not take up with anyone new until your elders have helped you see whether you are free to marry (WCF 24.5-6). If you find any of this in you, bring it to Christ, who died for sins like these and rose again. He turns away no one who comes, and he is faithful and just to forgive (1 John 1:9). If you are his, ask him for grace to forgive as you have been forgiven. If shame or grief brings thoughts of ending your life, call 988 or text 988 , and tell someone near you.

title: When Your Marriage Is Breaking
section: If you are the one who broke faith
text: If you are the one who broke faith After David took another man’s wife and had the man killed, he wrote this. The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise. Psalm 51:17 (KJV) A contrite heart is a crushed one. When Nathan confronted him, David said, I have sinned against the Lord . And Nathan said, The Lord also hath put away thy sin (2 Samuel 12:13). Christ died for sins like yours, and rose again. Tonight, tell God all of it, as David did. If you turn from your sin to Christ and confess it, God’s pardon is full at once. It rests on Christ’s blood, not on how well you confess (WCF 15.3). Your wife’s or husband’s trust is another matter. It comes back slowly, if at all, and it is theirs to give. You cannot make them trust you, or make them stay. Never use God’s forgiveness as a lever. Let your pastor or elders help you confess to your spouse without excuse (WCF 15.6). Bear the consequences. If your sin has made them afraid of you, give them the distance they ask for. There is more on forsaking this sin and fighting it under I have been unfaithful . If the shame tells you your family would be better off without you, that is a lie. Call 988 or text 988 tonight. And if this sin feels too great to forgive, read What I did is too great to forgive .

title: When Your Marriage Is Breaking
text: If it is your parents It is not your fault. Nothing you said or did caused this, and it is not your job to fix it. You may keep loving both of your parents. You never have to carry messages between them, or pick a side. Tell an adult you trust how you are really doing. That could be a parent, a teacher, a school counselor, or your pastor. David once wrote, When my father and my mother forsake me, then the Lord will take me up (Psalm 27:10). To take up is to take in, the way a family takes in a child who has nowhere else to go. David meant that even if his own parents failed him, God would not. If your parents’ divorce feels like that, and you trust him, this is God’s word to you. It is not a verdict on your parents. Jesus was left alone too. The night he was arrested, all his friends ran away. He died for sinners and rose again, and he never leaves anyone who trusts him. You can tell him exactly how you feel tonight, even if you are angry. If anyone at home is hurting you, get safe first . If you ever think of ending your life, call 988 or text 988 . If you do not know Christ, or are not sure you do, his own question is below .

title: When Your Child Walks Away From the Lord
text: You taught them to pray, and now they want nothing to do with Christ. You cannot give anyone a new heart. Only God can, and he has done it for sons and daughters as far off as yours.

title: When Your Child Walks Away From the Lord
section: When you are ready to search your heart
text: When you are ready to search your heart Your grief for your child is love, not sin, and this is not a hunt for a cause. Your child’s sin is their own. But a long sorrow has its own temptations, and it is a mercy to see them. One is despair, as if your child were beyond God’s reach. It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord (Lamentations 3:26). Another is a hard heart toward your child, the cold word, or the door shut in anger and not for safety. In Jesus’ story the elder brother was angry, and would not go in when his brother came home (Luke 15:28). Pray that if your child comes home, you will run like the father. Another is the opposite, handing over money that feeds their sin, or making excuses for it, and calling it love. Another is turning on your husband or wife, as if blame could bring your child home. And longing for your child’s return is right, but it can become the thing you live for, more than Christ himself. If you find any of these in you, bring it to Christ, who died for sins like these and rose again. He turns away no one who comes, and he is faithful and just to forgive (1 John 1:9). Then keep praying for your child by name. If you do not know Christ, or are not sure you do, his own question is below .

title: When You Lose Your Job or Home
text: The job or the business is gone, or the savings, or a fire or a flood took the house. It is hard to be the one who is supposed to provide. If you are his, your Father knows what you need.

title: When You Lose Your Job or Home
section: When you are ready to search your heart
text: When you are ready to search your heart This is not a hunt for the cause of your loss. It is a look at how you are bearing it, for want has temptations of its own. Fear can harden into distrust of God. You may envy those who kept what you lost. Asaph confessed, I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked (Psalm 73:3). Want can tempt you to cut a corner, or to chase quick money. Agur asked God for neither poverty nor riches, because he knew want could tempt him to steal (Proverbs 30:8-9). If an employer wronged you, seeking what you are owed is right, but do not let a grudge take root. Pride can refuse help, or refuse humbler work. Humble work is no fall. The Son of God worked with his hands as a carpenter (Mark 6:3). And the job may have been where you kept your worth. If you are his, your worth is kept in Christ, and no lost job can touch it. If you find any of this in you, bring it to Christ, who became poor for his people, died, and rose again. He turns away no one who comes, and he is faithful and just to forgive (1 John 1:9). Then ask for this day’s bread, and do the next thing. If you do not know Christ, or are not sure you do, his own question is below .

title: When You Are Lonely
text: The house is quiet, or the room is full and no one knows you. You may have been alone for years. Christ knew what it was to be left, and he has not left you.

title: When You Are Lonely
section: God Setteth the Solitary in Families
text: God Setteth the Solitary in Families God does not leave his people to be alone with him and no one else. The same psalm that calls him a father of the fatherless says, God setteth the solitary in families (Psalm 68:5-6). He does it through his church. Jesus said that whoever does the will of God is his brother, and sister, and mother (Mark 3:35). To those who leave house and family for his sake he promised houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, now in this time, with persecutions (Mark 10:29-30). Those are the people of God, and if you are his, they are given to you. Saints, by profession, are bound to maintain an holy fellowship and communion in the worship of God, and in performing such other spiritual services as tend to their mutual edification; as also in relieving each other in outward things, according to their several abilities and necessities. Westminster Confession of Faith 26.2 That bond is real before anyone feels it. A church will not always notice you without being told, and some of that is their sin. But you belong to them, and they to you. You may tell your elders that you are alone. That is not complaining. It lets the church obey.

title: When You Are Lonely
text: If You Are Single If you long to be married, the longing is not sin. God himself said, It is not good that the man should be alone (Genesis 2:18). But marriage is his gift to give, and he does not give it to every one of his people in this life. Paul was unmarried, and he said that every man hath his proper gift of God, one after this manner, and another after that (1 Corinthians 7:7). A single believer is not loved less by God than a married one. If you marry, marry only in the Lord (1 Corinthians 7:39). Loneliness is a poor counselor in that choice. Talk it over with your elders and with believers who know you.

title: When You Are Lonely
section: If You Are Married and Alone
text: If You Are Married and Alone You may share a house and a name with someone and still be alone. Your husband or wife may not believe, or may have grown cold, or may simply not speak of the things you most need to say. Peter wrote to wives whose husbands obey not the word (1 Peter 3:1), so God has not overlooked you. Tell your pastor. If you are afraid at home, get safe first . If your marriage is breaking, that has its own page .

title: When You Are Lonely
section: When you are ready to search your heart
text: When you are ready to search your heart Not tonight. Loneliness itself is not sin. It is an ache God made you able to feel, and Christ felt it. But a long loneliness opens doors, and it is a mercy to see them. Ask God to search you (Psalm 139:23). It can send you to a screen at night for company, or to pornography , or to drink . It can rush you toward someone who does not love the Lord. It can harden into self-pity, or into bitterness against a church that did not notice you. And it can keep you home from worship, the very place God gathers his people together. Elijah once told God, I, even I only, am left (1 Kings 19:10). God answered that he had kept seven thousand in Israel who had not bowed the knee to Baal (19:18). Your loneliness may tell you that no one else is faithful, or that no one cares. It may be wrong. If you find any of this in you, bring it to Christ, who was forsaken for sinners and rose again. He turns away no one who comes, and he is faithful and just to forgive (1 John 1:9). Then go to his people again this Lord’s Day, and sit near someone. If you do not know Christ, or are not sure you do, his own question is below .

title: When You Are Depressed
text: For weeks or years the heaviness has not lifted, or it keeps coming back. Sleep does not rest you, and the promises you once loved seem to belong to someone else. Christ has been in the dark before you.

title: When You Are Depressed
section: When you are ready to search your heart
text: When you are ready to search your heart Do this in a better hour, and not alone if you can help it. It is not a hunt for a sin behind the dark (John 9:3). For you, the searching should be short and the looking to Christ long. Who is among you that feareth the Lord , that obeyeth the voice of his servant, that walketh in darkness, and hath no light? let him trust in the name of the Lord , and stay upon his God. Isaiah 50:10 (KJV) To stay upon God is to lean your whole weight on him. Watch for only a few things. The dark may tempt you to give up the Word, prayer, and worship, because they feel empty. Keep to them, even briefly, and let others pray with you. It may tempt you to dull the pain with drink or drugs , or to hide how bad it is. If the dark tells you that God will never be kind to you again, it is lying. If the dark tells you that others would be better off without you, that is a lie too. If thoughts of ending your life come, stop the searching and get help now. Do not keep them secret. Call 988 or text 988 , and tell someone near you. Where you find sin, confess it simply. Christ died for sinners and rose again, and he turns away no one who comes. So look away from yourself to him. If you do not know Christ, or are not sure you do, his own question is below .

title: If You Are Not Safe
text: Some hard hours are dangerous. If yours is, the first faithful thing to do is to get safe. Read the rest later.

title: If You Are Not Safe
section: If you are thinking of ending your life
text: If you are thinking of ending your life Do not wait for morning, and do not wait until you can explain it well. Call 988 or text 988 , and then tell someone safe near you tonight, a husband or wife, a parent, a friend, or your pastor. If the means to end your life are near you, give them to someone to keep tonight, or put them where you cannot reach them. Your life is not yours to end. It belongs to the Lord who made you. If you are Christ’s, it is his twice over, for ye are bought with a price (1 Corinthians 6:20). He died and rose for you, and he has not finished with your life. The Larger Catechism counts it a duty of the sixth commandment to preserve our own lives as well as the lives of others (Q&A 135). When Elijah asked God to take his life, God sent him sleep and bread, and then work to do (1 Kings 19). Asking for help is not weakness. It is obedience.

title: If You Are Not Safe
text: If someone is hurting you For he shall deliver the needy when he crieth; the poor also, and him that hath no helper. He shall spare the poor and needy, and shall save the souls of the needy. He shall redeem their soul from deceit and violence: and precious shall their blood be in his sight. Psalm 72:12-14 (KJV) This is a psalm about the true King, and Christ is that King. He is not neutral about what is being done to you. If a husband or a wife or anyone in your home hits you, threatens you, forces you, or makes you afraid for your life or your children, you may leave to be safe, and you should. The Larger Catechism names just defense against violence, and protecting and defending the innocent, among the duties God requires (Q&A 135). Scripture says a prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself (Proverbs 22:3). When Saul threw a javelin at David, David fled, and his wife let him down through a window (1 Samuel 19:10-12). Jesus told his disciples that when they were persecuted in one city, they should flee into another (Matthew 10:23). Leaving to be safe is not a lack of faith, and it is not a sin. You are not to blame for another person’s violence. Questions about the marriage itself can wait, and your elders can help you with them later. Calling the police is not revenge, and it is not a betrayal of the church. Scripture calls the ruler the minister of God, who bears the sword against those who do evil (Romans 13:4). Tell your elders too, once you are safe. If the one hurting you is an elder, or close to one, tell another pastor you trust. If anyone tells you to go back into danger, do not go back. Go to the police, and find a pastor who will stand with you. Christ is the Bridegroom who gave himself for his bride, and who nourishes and cherishes her (Ephesians 5:25, 29). What is being done to you is the opposite of what he does. When a crowd at Nazareth tried to throw him off a cliff, he passed through the midst of them and went his way (Luke 4:29-30). His hour had not yet come. When it came, he gave himself up on the cross, of his own will and in the place of sinners, and on the third day he rose. That work is finished. Your suffering cannot add to it, so you are not called to stay under violence.

title: If You Are Not Safe
section: If a child is being hurt
text: If a child is being hurt If a child is in danger, call 911 now. Otherwise report it to the police or to your county’s child protective services, and Childhelp can tell you how. Do not wait for anyone at church to handle it first. Abuse is a crime, and God gave the civil ruler the sword to punish it. A faithful church will stand with you when you call. If you are young and someone is hurting you, tell a teacher or a school counselor today. If you are in danger right now, call 911 , and you can call Childhelp at 1-800-422-4453 at any hour. They are trained for this, and the law requires them to act.

title: Struggling With Sin
text: For anyone worn down by a sin that will not let go. A heart gives up an old love only for a stronger one, and Christ is the one love strong enough to drive the others out.

title: Struggling With Sin
section: If You Are Tired of Losing
text: Read this first If You Are Tired of Losing You may have fought this sin for years. You may be ashamed to make God the same promise one more time. This page is for you, and it does not begin with a new promise. If your sin is hurting another person, especially a child, it stops now. Read My sin is hurting someone else before anything else. In danger, or thinking of ending your life? Call 911 , or call 988 or text 988 , now, and tell someone near you. If someone is hurting you, read If You Are Not Safe . Outside the United States, call your local emergency number. If you write to me about your sin, know first that I cannot keep a secret that leaves someone in danger. If your sin is hurting a child or anyone else, go to your pastor and the authorities before you write to me. Most of us tell God we are done with a sin, and for a while the promise holds. Then a bad night comes, and the old sin walks back in as if it still had a key. A sin keeps its hold because the heart still loves it. So this page begins with what you love, and with the King you are coming to, who will not break a bruised reed (Isaiah 42:3). If you are not sure you have ever come to Christ, read Where the Fight Begins first. If you are near despair, go straight to The Ground Under Your Feet . If there is a sin you love and mean to keep, there is an honest word for you too. If you already use Mortify and temptation is on you right now, open it and press Flee, and come back to this page when the hour has passed. If what troubles you is a thought you hate and never chose, read Doubts and Unwanted Thoughts first, because a page like this can feed that fear. For you, the searching should be short and the looking to Christ long.

title: Struggling With Sin
text: The root The Heart Is Never Empty Sin breaks God’s law, and at its root it is love turned from God to something else. That is why a promise to stop so seldom holds. The Westminster Shorter Catechism, part of the standard this site holds , begins with what you were made for. Man’s chief end is to glorify God, and to enjoy him for ever. Westminster Shorter Catechism Q&A 1 So your heart was built to want, and it never stops wanting. The wanting itself is God’s gift, and sin has bent it. God named what we do instead through Jeremiah. For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water. Jeremiah 2:13 (KJV) A cistern was a pit cut in rock to catch the rain, and a broken one leaks. The sin you keep going back to is a cistern you dug. It promised rest after a hard day, or the feeling of being wanted, and it never held. Paul calls covetousness idolatry, love given to something that should never have had it, and in the same verse he names the bent desires that must be put to death (Colossians 3:5). So proving to a man that his sin is empty seldom sets him free. He has known it every morning after. Thomas Chalmers, a Scottish minister, preached on this two hundred years ago in a sermon called The Expulsive Power of a New Affection. An affection is what the heart loves and leans toward, and expulsive means driving out. The heart must have something to cling to, he said, and the only way to dispossess it of an old affection is by the expulsive power of a new one. Jesus told of a house swept clean and left empty, and of what came back to fill it (Matthew 12:43-45). Nobody blows out his candle because someone proves it is small. He sets it down when the sun is up. Chalmers did not mean that any new interest will do. The love that drives out the love of the world, he said, arises only when by faith a man sees God’s glory in the face of Jesus Christ and hears him call all who will to a full pardon. Willpower can sweep the house. It cannot fill it.

title: Struggling With Sin
text: A greater affection Beholding Christ The one love strong enough to drive out the others is love for Christ, and it grows from seeing his love for sinners. God does not ask you to work it up. He shows you his Son. But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord. 2 Corinthians 3:18 (KJV) A glass is a mirror, and the mirror is the gospel, which shows the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ (2 Corinthians 4:6). We become like what we behold, slowly, and the Spirit does it. Paul says this of everyone whose heart has turned to the Lord (3:16), and it can begin for you the day you turn. Beholding him does not mean picturing his face (Larger Catechism Q&A 109). It means looking by faith at who Scripture shows him to be and what he does. Read the Gospels slowly, and watch him touch a leper (Mark 1:41) and eat with sinners (Luke 15:2). Sit under preaching that holds him out, and if you are a communing member of a faithful church, come to his Table. God grows a new love by these ordinary means. He offered the woman at the well living water before she had changed anything, though her life was a row of broken cisterns (John 4:13-18). He offers the same water to you. And where his pardon is known, love follows. Of the woman who wept at his feet he said, Her sins, which are many, are forgiven (Luke 7:47). Her love was the fruit of that pardon, and it was her faith that saved her (7:50). We love him, because he first loved us (1 John 4:19). John Owen, an English Puritan pastor, gave the same counsel in his book Indwelling Sin, to fill your affections with the cross of Christ, that there may be no room for sin. This is no technique, and no feeling you must produce before you may fight.

title: Struggling With Sin
text: If you are not his yet Where the Fight Begins Only those who belong to Christ can put sin to death. If you are not his yet, your fight begins with him. Mortify means to put to death. Before Owen gave a single direction for doing it, he said that unless a man is truly joined to Christ, he can never mortify any one sin. Paul says that if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his (Romans 8:9). So conversion comes first, and Owen said that is no unkindness. If a man is patching a hole in his wall while the whole house burns, the friend who calls him to the fire is not his enemy. Sin is a master, and only the Son can make you free indeed (John 8:34-36). He lived the life you have not lived. He bore the curse in the place of all who trust him, and he rose again. He is freely offered to you, and he turns away no one who comes. If your sin is harming someone, stop today and get help ( My sin is hurting someone else ). Stopping is right, and it still cannot make you his. The promises further down this page belong to those who belong to Christ. They can be yours. Come to Him tells you how.

title: Struggling With Sin
text: Mortification Putting Sin to Death Once the heart has seen Christ, it turns against the old love that still pulls at it, and the Spirit gives it strength to put that sin to death. Paul joins what you love to what you do, and the hinge is one word. If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God. Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth. For ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God. When Christ, who is our life, shall appear, then shall ye also appear with him in glory. Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry: Colossians 3:1-5 (KJV) Mortify means put to death. The therefore in verse 5 hangs on verses 1 to 4. If you are his, you died with Christ and your life is hid with him in God, and so you are to set your heart on things above. Only then does Paul say, Mortify. Inordinate affection is love out of order, and concupiscence is evil desire. The members to mortify are the sins in Paul’s list, not the limbs of the body. Jesus spoke the same way when he said to pluck out a right eye, or cut off a right hand, that offends, which means one that makes you stumble (Matthew 5:29-30). He had just put lust in the heart (5:28), and a man with one eye can still lust. It is a picture of cutting off whatever feeds the sin, even what you value most. God never asks you to harm your body (Larger Catechism Q&A 135-136), and if you are his, your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost (1 Corinthians 6:19). If you have hurt yourself, or feel driven to, call 988 or text 988 now. If you are badly hurt, call 911 . In 1656 Owen wrote Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, a book Christians have leaned on ever since, and he built it on one verse. For if ye live after the flesh, ye shall die: but if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live. Romans 8:13 (KJV) Ye means believers, who are under no condemnation (Romans 8:1). The flesh is the old sinful nature, not skin and bone. Ye do mortify means the work is yours, and through the Spirit means the strength is his. The if shows the path the believer walks. It does not set a price on life, for Christ has already paid that for all who are his. Owen said that even the best believers must make this their business all their days. As he put it, be killing sin or it will be killing you. They who are once effectually called and regenerated, having a new heart and a new spirit created in them, are further sanctified, really and personally, through the virtue of Christ’s death and resurrection, by his Word and Spirit dwelling in them; the dominion of the whole body of sin is destroyed, and the several lusts thereof are more and more weakened and mortified, and they more and more quickened and strengthened, in all saving graces, to the practice of true holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord. Westminster Confession of Faith 13.1 Quickened means made alive, virtue means power, and a lust is any strong sinful desire. Saving graces are the holy habits the Spirit grows in God’s people, such as faith and humility. Notice the words more and more. The change is real and slow, and never finished in this life (Westminster Confession 13.2). Owen warned that a calm temper, a hidden sin, or a burst of zeal after a scare kills nothing, and that the man who trades one sin for another hath changed his master, but is a servant still. The real thing is slower. Owen pictured a man nailed to a cross, who cries out loudly at first and more faintly as his blood drains away. He took the picture from Paul, who says, They that are Christ’s have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts (Galatians 5:24). Sin in a believer dies that way, slowly, more and more as the Confession says, and never all the way in this life. All that while, a new grace grows in its place. Owen also asked why you fight. True mortification, he said, rests on hating sin because it is sin, and not only because it shames you, and on a sense of Christ’s love shown at the cross.

title: Struggling With Sin
text: The daily work How the Fight Is Fought The Spirit does not do this in your place, and you cannot do it without him. The Confession holds both together. Their ability to do good works is not at all of themselves, but wholly from the Spirit of Christ. And that they may be enabled thereunto, besides the graces they have already received, there is required an actual influence of the same Holy Spirit to work in them to will and to do of his good pleasure; yet are they not hereupon to grow negligent, as if they were not bound to perform any duty unless upon a special motion of the Spirit; but they ought to be diligent in stirring up the grace of God that is in them. Westminster Confession of Faith 16.3 A special motion means a special stirring. Some teach that a Christian should stop trying and let God do it, and the Confession will not have it. Owen said of the Spirit that he works in us and with us, not against us or without us. God works in, so you work out (Philippians 2:12-13), and work out never means work for. If you are his, do these things, and begin each day with the first. Look to Christ before you look at the sin. Owen’s chief direction for killing sin was to set faith at work on Christ, and he called Christ’s blood the great sovereign remedy for sin-sick souls. Come to the throne of grace for mercy for the last fall and grace for the next hour (Hebrews 4:16). Strike at the first stirring. A man is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed, before the desire ever conceives and brings forth sin (James 1:14-15). Strike before it conceives. Cut off what feeds it. Make not provision for the flesh (Romans 13:14). With each sin God forbids all the causes, means, occasions, and appearances thereof (Larger Catechism Q&A 99). Put the phone out of the bedroom at night, take a different road home, and end the friendship that keeps leading you back. When you must, run. Joseph left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out (Genesis 39:12). Bring it into the light. The Confession asks you to repent of your particular sins particularly (15.5). That means naming this sin to God plainly, and then being done. It does not mean listing every passing thought. Then tell a believer you trust, a man if you are a man and a woman if you are a woman, or tell your elders, because sin deceives and God’s remedy is to exhort one another daily (Hebrews 3:13). If you are young, tell a parent, or if you cannot, another adult you trust, such as a teacher or your pastor. If you are the pastor, tell an elder or a minister you trust. Keep to the means. Watch and pray (Matthew 26:41). Put your baptism to use by drawing strength from the death and resurrection of Christ, into whom we are baptized, for the mortifying of sin (Larger Catechism Q&A 167). Sit under the Word in a church, and not only on a screen, and if you are a communing member, come to the Table ( The Life That Comes After ).

title: Struggling With Sin
section: Return, ye backsliding children, and I will heal your backslidings. Behold, we come unto thee; for thou art the LORD our God.
text: Mortify, a help for the daily work Return, ye backsliding children, and I will heal your backslidings. Behold, we come unto thee; for thou art the LORD our God. Jeremiah 3:22 (KJV) I made a free app for the work this page describes. It goes where you go, so the help is in your hand in the hour you need it. Mortify Free · Works in any browser · Sign up to begin Open it on your phone and add it to your home screen. Then it opens like an app. Open Mortify See all it does When temptation comes, open it and press Flee. Choose the sin you are fighting, and it sets before you Scripture for that sin, a word from a Puritan such as John Owen or Thomas Watson, a prayer, and something to do right now. For lust at a screen, it may tell you to put the phone in another room, or to get up and go where people are. Each morning there is a reading, and each night a few honest questions about the day. After a fall it does not scold you. It turns you back to Christ. Mortify’s own page tells all it does. It is a help and not a Savior. It cannot fight in your place, and it does not stand in for Christ, his Word, or your church.

title: Struggling With Sin
section: When the Sin Has a Name
text: Particular sins When the Sin Has a Name Some sins bring danger with them, to you or to someone near you. They are fought the same way at the root, with your eyes on Christ, and they need more help than a page can give. If none of these is yours, go on to The Ground Under Your Feet . Two things first. If you cut or starve or purge yourself, see a doctor this week, and if you feel driven to hurt yourself, call 988 or text 988 now. And what was done to you by force, or by an adult when you were a child, is not your sin to put to death ( If You Are Not Safe ). I cannot stop looking at what I should not If these are thoughts you hate and never chose, this section is not for you. Go to Doubts and Unwanted Thoughts . If it is pornography, name it to yourself and to God. Christ was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin (Hebrews 4:15), and there is grace to help at his throne (4:16). Put the screen out of reach at the hours you fall, and tell someone. If you are young, tell a parent, or if you cannot, another adult you trust. If you are married, ask your pastor or an elder to help you bring it into the light at home. If you are an adult and what you look at shows anyone under eighteen, a real child was abused to make it, and looking at it is a crime. Stop today, and read My sin is hurting someone else . If you are young and an adult showed you these things or asked you for pictures, or if anyone at any age threatens to share pictures of you, it is being done to you. Do not pay, and do not send more. Stop answering, and do not delete the messages. If you are young, tell a parent or another adult you trust today. If you are grown, tell the police. If it feels like more than you can live through, call 988 or text 988 . I have been unfaithful If it is still going on, end it today, with no contact, as Joseph fled (Genesis 39:12). If the affair was physical, see a doctor and be tested, for your husband’s or wife’s sake as well as your own. For confessing to your husband or wife, read If you are the one who broke faith . If you catch yourself thinking your family would be better off without you, that is a lie. Call 988 or text 988 . My anger frightens my family A harsh husband or wife, father or mother, is the opposite of the gentle King, and tears after an outburst are not yet repentance. If you have hit, choked, forced, or threatened anyone at home, or broken things to frighten them, that is abuse and a crime. Give them the distance they ask for. Do not press them to forgive you, to take back what they told anyone, or to sit in counseling with you. Tell your elders, and accept that the police may be involved. If you are afraid you will hurt someone, leave the house and call 911 . Give any guns in the house to someone to keep. If you are the one who is afraid, read If You Are Not Safe . Drink or drugs have hold of me Paul sets a better filling against drink, Be filled with the Spirit (Ephesians 5:18). God works through means (Westminster Confession 5.3), and a doctor and treatment are among them. If you drink heavily every day, or take a pill like Xanax or Valium every day, do not stop all at once on your own, since that can bring seizures and can kill. See a doctor this week, tell the whole truth about how much you use, and let someone go with you. Tell your pastor or an elder too. After even a few days off opioids, your old dose can kill you. If someone has taken too much, call 911 , and give naloxone (Narcan) if you have it. Do not stop a prescribed medicine without asking your doctor. My sin is hurting someone else If these are thoughts you hate and never chose, this section is not for you. Go to Doubts and Unwanted Thoughts . If you have not acted, but you fear a desire toward a child, do not be alone with children, and tell a doctor and your pastor this week. A doctor can tell a fear you hate from a desire you must fight, and there is help for both. If you have harmed someone, the harm stops first. If it touches a child, stay away from children today, your own included. If the child lives with you, you are the one who leaves the house, today. Do not ask the child or anyone in the family to keep it quiet. Tell your pastor, and know that harm to a child must be reported to the police or to child protective services. A faithful church will not keep it secret. Accept what the law does (Romans 13:4), for pardon with God does not cancel earthly justice. Christ turns away no one who comes to him, and coming to him means coming into the light, for he that doeth truth cometh to the light (John 3:21). This hour is dangerous for your own life too. If you are thinking of ending it, call 988 or text 988 now.

title: Struggling With Sin
text: Assurance The Ground Under Your Feet If you are his, you do not fight for your place with God. You fight from it. Justification is God’s verdict that pardons a sinner and counts him righteous for Christ’s sake. Sanctification is his lifelong work of making that sinner holy. The Larger Catechism sets them side by side. Although sanctification be inseparably joined with justification, yet they differ, in that God in justification imputeth the righteousness of Christ; in sanctification his Spirit infuseth grace, and enableth to the exercise thereof; in the former, sin is pardoned; in the other, it is subdued: the one doth equally free all believers from the revenging wrath of God, and that perfectly in this life, that they never fall into condemnation; the other is neither equal in all, nor in this life perfect in any, but growing up to perfection. Westminster Larger Catechism Q&A 77 Imputeth means credits to your account, and infuseth means pours in. The pardon is the same in every believer and perfect today, whatever your week was like. The subduing of sin is uneven in all and finished in none. Your standing rests on the first, and the second is the evidence that you have it ( Justification by Faith Alone ). A boy who breaks a window is in trouble with his father, but he is not an orphan again. The Confession gives assurance three grounds, God’s promises first, then the graces he works in his children, then his Spirit’s witness ( Am I Really Saved? ). In Grace Abounding, John Bunyan tells how he saw that his good frame of heart did not make his righteousness before God better, nor his bad frame make it worse. He wrote, my righteousness was Jesus Christ Himself. It can seem wiser to keep a struggling Christian unsure, as if fear would keep him careful. The Confession says the opposite. God settles his children’s place in his house before he sends them out to fight, and he wants them sure of it. A true believer may wait long and fight hard before he has that assurance, so if you lack it, that does not prove you are not his. Seek it all the same, for the Confession calls that seeking a duty, and assurance makes a Christian stronger in the fight and never looser. This infallible assurance doth not so belong to the essence of faith, but that a true believer may wait long, and conflict with many difficulties before he be partaker of it: yet, being enabled by the Spirit to know the things which are freely given him of God, he may, without extraordinary revelation, in the right use of ordinary means, attain thereunto. And therefore it is the duty of every one to give all diligence to make his calling and election sure; that thereby his heart may be enlarged in peace and joy in the Holy Ghost, in love and thankfulness to God, and in strength and cheerfulness in the duties of obedience, the proper fruits of this assurance: so far is it from inclining men to looseness. Westminster Confession of Faith 18.3 Looseness means careless living. So Paul promises all who are under grace, For sin shall not have dominion over you, and he gives the reason, for ye are not under the law, but under grace (Romans 6:14). A hired hand works in dread of losing his place, and that slavish fear, as the Confession calls it (20.1), never taught a heart to love. A son works his father’s field because it is his father’s. His fear is a son’s fear of grieving the father who loves him, and in that fear believers go on perfecting holiness (2 Corinthians 7:1). I fell again today Then go back to Christ tonight, with the sin still on your hands. Micah spoke for God’s people when they were brought low for their sin. When I fall, I shall arise, he says, and in the next breath, I have sinned against him (Micah 7:8-9). After Peter denied him, the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter (Luke 22:61), and Peter wept and was restored. Judas was sorry too (Matthew 27:3), but he carried his sorrow away from Christ, and Paul calls that the sorrow of the world (2 Corinthians 7:10). Whatever your sorrow tells you, carry it to him. One grave sin can shake your assurance for a while, yet the seed of God remains in his children (Westminster Confession 18.4, and see When God Feels Far ). Confess it, for he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins (1 John 1:9). If you fear he must be tired of forgiving you, read When the Same Sin Keeps Coming Back . If the shame tells you that you would be better off dead, or that others would be better off without you, it is lying. Call 988 or text 988 now, and tell someone near you. I do not feel that I love him If you cannot feel your love for him, but you long to be free of your sin and to love him more, look at the longing itself. Owen said that longing, breathing, and panting after deliverance is a grace in itself. Peter wrote to believers, Whom having not seen, ye love (1 Peter 1:8), and the Larger Catechism (Q&A 172) asks what you want, not whether you have won yet . You must truly be Christ’s to put sin to death, Owen said. But you need not first be sure that you are, for a true believer may wait long before he has that assurance (Westminster Confession 18.3). Your hope rests on Christ and his promise, not on how the fight is going, though the fight itself is one of the marks of his Spirit in you. So look to Christ, and fight. Richard Sibbes wrote in The Bruised Reed that there is more mercy in Christ than sin in us.

title: Struggling With Sin
section: If You Have Made Peace With It
text: An honest word If You Have Made Peace With It This part is not for the one who hates his sin and keeps losing. It is for the one who has stopped fighting and made a home for it. If you hate your sin, even as you fall, go on to the last section . If reading this frightens you and makes you want to fight, it is not describing you. Go on too. The first half of Romans 8:13 is a real warning to the church. If ye live after the flesh, ye shall die. Owen said that a man who finds no fight in himself against his sin, and does not set himself against it, is at peace with it, not dying to it. Although hypocrites and other unregenerate men may vainly deceive themselves with false hopes and carnal presumptions of being in the favour of God and estate of salvation, which hope of theirs shall perish: yet such as truly believe in the Lord Jesus, and love him in sincerity, endeavouring to walk in all good conscience before him, may in this life be certainly assured that they are in the state of grace, and may rejoice in the hope of the glory of God, which hope shall never make them ashamed. Westminster Confession of Faith 18.1 Carnal presumptions are hopes the sinful heart takes for granted. One hope shall perish and the other shall never make them ashamed. What divides them is a true faith in the Lord Jesus, with the sincere love for him and the honest effort to walk with him that always come with it. If you love a sin and mean to keep it, you have no ground to call yourself safe, whatever you once prayed or professed. God’s foundation carries two sayings on one seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his, and, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity (2 Timothy 2:19). That is hard to hear. It is said plainly because the door is still open. Go to your elders and tell them the truth. Paul says, Let a man examine himself, and so let him eat (1 Corinthians 11:28), and a man who means to keep his sin should not come to the Table until he has turned from it (Westminster Confession 29.8). Christ has given his church the power to keep such a man from the Table until he turns (Larger Catechism Q&A 173). That discipline is care that aims to bring you back ( Where Christ Feeds His People ). Owen’s rule, that only a believer can put sin to death, reaches you too. If you will not fight, you may need to come to Christ as if for the first time, and you may come today. The goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance (Romans 2:4).

title: Struggling With Sin
text: The end of the fight Until You See Him For all who are his, this fight has an end. The last look at Christ will finish what the first look began. Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is. And every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself, even as he is pure. 1 John 3:2-3 (KJV) Beholding him by faith changes us slowly now, and seeing him will finish it. At death the souls of believers are made perfect in holiness ( Afraid of Dying ), and the sin you have fought will not come with you. If you are his, take the same road again tomorrow. The King you fight under will not break a bruised reed (Matthew 12:20). Of faith set on Christ, Owen wrote, live in this, and thou wilt die a conqueror. If you are not his yet, all of this can be yours. Christ died for sinners and rose again, and he is freely offered to you. He is gentle with those who come. Turn from your sin and trust him. Come as you are, today, and he will do the cleaning. Let your elders know you, and if you have no church, find a faithful one. If you would like someone to pray for you, write to me . I am not a pastor, so in an emergency do not wait on me. Come to Him

title: Doctrine
text: Explore Reformed doctrine one subject at a time, from Scripture to the things to come.

title: Doctrine
text: Begin With One Subject Doctrine teaches us who God is and what he has done. Start with the Word of God, or choose the subject you need. Each page keeps the fuller teaching and its Scripture references. Why Doctrine Matters Why sound teaching belongs to the Christian life. The Bible Why Scripture is our final rule of faith and life. God and the Trinity The one living God, Father, Son, and Holy Ghost. The Five Solas Salvation by grace alone through faith alone in Christ alone.
