Come feel God’s presence,” and he has urged them not to “idolize a preacher.” He has told visitors from other cities to go home and “find a Bible teaching church where the word of God is being communicated.” In April 2025 a sermon of his told Black parents to “stop blaming white cops for the killing of Black kids,” and it caused deep grief. He publicly apologized and said his framing “was and is harmful.” Not every preacher with his following is willing to do that. These strengths are real, and they help explain why so many young people have been stirred by his preaching. They also explain why his errors are dangerous. Error rarely comes to the table alone. It usually comes on the same plate as truth, and the truth makes it easier to swallow.

title: Philip Anthony Mitchell
text: The Person of Christ The most serious finding concerns the doctrine of Christ. In “Stay Awake,” a sermon on Matthew 24:36-51 published August 11, 2025, Mitchell took up the question of how Jesus could say he did not know the day of his return. About seventeen minutes in, the published transcript records these words. His own words. “Christ, when he was on the earth, was fully God and fully human at the same time. … if he’s God, he is all-knowing. … I think the canosis of Philippians 2 solves this question. … he emptied himself, the canosis in Greek, of some of his divine nature, so that he can fully step into human. … The evidence that he emptied himself is that he needed to pray just like you.” “Stay Awake,” Matthew 24:36-51, about 16 to 18 minutes. “Canosis” is the transcript’s spelling of the Greek word kenosis. A few minutes later, about twenty-two minutes in, he adds, “I do believe now that he’s seated at the right hand of the father he probably knows the day and the hour.” That line confirms what he meant. He believes the Son gave up his divine knowledge for a time and has it again now. This view is called kenotic Christology. It teaches that the eternal Son laid aside some of his divine attributes in order to become man. The text Mitchell leaned on doesn’t say that. Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: but made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men: Philippians 2:5-7 (KJV) The words “made himself of no reputation” stand for the Greek word Mitchell reached for, which many newer Bibles put as “emptied himself.” But look at how Paul says it was done. The Son made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant. He humbled himself by taking something. He added a true human nature to the divine nature he always had. He veiled the outward blaze of his glory and stooped to the lowest place, all the way to the cross. He didn’t subtract any part of his Godhead, and he couldn’t have. Deity has no parts to give away, and God doesn’t change. If the Son gave up some of his divine nature, then the One who walked in Galilee was something less than God. For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily. Colossians 2:9 (KJV) The Westminster Confession states the church’s settled faith with great care. The Son of God, the second person in the Trinity, being very and eternal God, of one substance, and equal with the Father, did, when the fulness of time was come, take upon him man’s nature, with all the essential properties and common infirmities thereof, yet without sin; being conceived by the power of the Holy Ghost, in the womb of the Virgin Mary, of her substance. So that two whole, perfect, and distinct natures, the Godhead and the manhood, were inseparably joined together in one person, without conversion, composition, or confusion. Which person is very God, and very man, yet one Christ, the only Mediator between God and man. Westminster Confession of Faith 8.2 So how could the Son say he did not know the day? The Reformed answer, with Calvin and the older church, is that Christ spoke according to his human nature. His human mind was a true human mind. It grew and learned, just as Luke tells us. And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man. Luke 2:52 (KJV) But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only. Matthew 24:36 (KJV) As God, the Son knew all things, even while he lay in the manger. As man, he learned and grew. Both are true of one Person, and neither nature was traded away for the other. That’s how Jesus could pray, hunger, and grow weary while he upheld all things by the word of his power. Mitchell is right that Christ’s prayer life shows his true humanity. He is wrong that the Son emptied himself “of some of his divine nature,” and that error sits at the foundation of the faith. Charity requires us to notice that Mitchell said in the same breath that Christ was fully God, and his church’s written statement confesses the same. The fairest reading is that he is confused, and not that he means to deny the deity of Christ. But a confused account of who Jesus is, preached to a vast audience and left standing, is a grave matter all the same. A man who titled his book Contend ought to be the first to contend here. This research found no public correction of this teaching. Because the transcript is made by machine, any believer who wants to confirm the wording can listen to “Stay Awake” on the 2819 Church podcast at about the seventeen minute mark. The wording is clear, and the later line about Christ knowing the day “now” only makes sense if he meant what the first line says.

title: Philip Anthony Mitchell
section: Claims of Direct Words From God
text: Claims of Direct Words From God Mitchell often speaks of God charging him and telling him things directly. The clearest example is his account of Israel in December 2018. In a sermon titled “A Clarion Call” he describes a man in Israel who laid hands on him and prayed over him. His own words. “He says, receive a double anointed [anointing] and lays his hands on me. And prays over me. … God charge you. Go back to your nation. … I’ve been charged by God almighty in the holy land of Israel.” “A Clarion Call,” about 28 to 29 minutes. Later in the same sermon he says, “And I can hear God telling me, man, there’s a work for you to do over here, my son.” The pattern runs through other sources too. The Associated Press reported in December 2025 that Mitchell “said God told him to preach without bringing prepared notes onstage.” In a sermon on faith he described “using my mouth in prayer and prophecy to agree with everything God already told me.” Speaking of the worship planned for ACCESS, he said, “I feel that in my spirit.” To his credit, he also warns against careless talk. In that same Israel sermon he said, “God said, two dangerous words,” and added, “Anytime I hear somebody say, God said, I’ve got a question, an eyebrow raised.” The trouble is that he doesn’t hold his own claims to that warning. God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds; Hebrews 1:1-2 (KJV) All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: that the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works. 2 Timothy 3:16-17 (KJV) The Westminster Confession says Holy Scripture is most necessary, “those former ways of God’s revealing his will unto his people being now ceased” (WCF 1.1). It also says that to the whole counsel of God set down in Scripture “nothing at any time is to be added, whether by new revelations of the Spirit, or traditions of men” (WCF 1.6). Reformed Christians don’t deny that God guides his people today. He guides by his Word, by his providence, and by wise counsel, and the Spirit opens our eyes to the Scriptures. A man may come home from Israel with a heavy burden for his nation, and God may use that burden greatly. What Scripture does not give us is fresh speech from God that carries his authority. When a preacher says “God told me,” his hearers rightly take him to mean that God has spoken. If God did not speak, then the claim puts words in God’s mouth. If God did speak, then his word binds the hearer just as the Bible does. Either way the claim is far heavier than charismatic preachers usually treat it. The practical danger is authority. In a 2025 sermon Mitchell told his church, “If you don’t like the vessel, pray for the vessel, especially if God sent the vessel.” A ministry whose founding story rests on a personal charge from God is very hard to correct, because a brother who questions the preacher seems to be questioning the God who sent him. Scripture gives every believer a better rule. Despise not prophesyings. Prove all things; hold fast that which is good. 1 Thessalonians 5:20-21 (KJV)

title: Philip Anthony Mitchell
section: Prayer, Portals, and a Demand on God
text: Prayer, Portals, and a Demand on God In “Expectations for ACCESS,” published in October 2025, Mitchell prepared his church for the Atlanta gathering. He rightly said that ACCESS “is a gathering of prayer” and that he named it for the access believers have in prayer. Then, about thirty-seven minutes in, he described the event this way. His own words. “We’re going to make the arena a portal from earth to heaven. … we will put a demand on him to come down.” “Expectations for ACCESS,” about 36 to 39 minutes. He also told them to expect “spiritual healing” and “even physical healing,” and he prayed for “signs and wonders and miracles and healing and deliverance.” Talk of portals and of placing a demand on heaven comes from the charismatic revival culture of open heavens and spiritual atmospheres. It has no place in Christian prayer. Believers already have access to the Father, and they have it in every place, because Christ opened the way by his own blood. Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus, by a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh; Hebrews 10:19-20 (KJV) A stadium is no nearer to heaven than a farmhouse kitchen. Jesus said as much to the woman at the well. Jesus saith unto her, Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father. … But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth: for the Father seeketh such to worship him. John 4:21, 23 (KJV) Neither prayer, nor any other part of religious worship, is now, under the gospel, either tied unto, or made more acceptable by any place in which it is performed, or towards which it is directed: but God is to be worshipped everywhere, in spirit and truth. Westminster Confession of Faith 21.6 No man puts a demand on God. We come as children who ask, and our Father gives according to his will. But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking. Be not ye therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him. Matthew 6:7-8 (KJV) And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us: 1 John 5:14 (KJV) The irony is painful. The gathering is named ACCESS, and access to God is exactly what Christ purchased for every believer in every room at every hour. Telling thousands of young Christians that a packed arena can become a portal draws them away from the closet and the Lord’s Day assembly, which are the places God has promised to meet them. Mitchell did say he wants people to pray in God’s will, and he isn’t teaching occult ritual. But the words he chose teach a wrong idea of prayer, and the crowd hears the words.

title: Philip Anthony Mitchell
section: Fasting and Promises God Did Not Make
text: Fasting and Promises God Did Not Make In January 2025 Mitchell called 2819 Church to a week of fasting in a sermon titled “So We Fasted,” from Ezra 8:21-23. He said, “For the majority of us, 85%, 90%, I’m calling you to what’s called a total fast,” and for himself, “water only.” He did offer a partial fast as another path. Fasting is biblical, and the Westminster Confession counts “solemn fastings” among the proper parts of worship upon special occasions (WCF 21.5). A pastor may rightly call his flock to humble themselves before God. The trouble lies in what Mitchell said fasting does. His own words. “I will weaken you so that who I really am, a spirit inside of a body can grow strong in intimacy with Christ. … When you fast, you hear God more clearly. … When you fast, you can move God to intervene in circumstances. … You’re going to be radically transformed. Your bodies are going to be healed.” “So We Fasted,” Ezra 8:21-23, about 15 and 48 minutes. Several problems stand out. The picture of a man as “a spirit inside of a body” isn’t how Scripture speaks. God made man a unity of body and soul, and the body is his good creation. The phrase echoes a saying the Word of Faith teachers made popular, that man is a spirit who has a soul and lives in a body. Fasting also doesn’t “move God” as though our hunger pulls a lever in heaven. God answers prayer freely, out of his own fatherly goodness. Worst of all, Mitchell promised a congregation that their bodies would be healed. God made no such promise. When that promise fails, the weak are left to wonder whether their faith or their fast was too small. Scripture warns that hard treatment of the body can look like wisdom and still leave sin untouched. Sin is put to death by the Spirit, through faith in Christ. Which things have indeed a shew of wisdom in will worship, and humility, and neglecting of the body; not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh. Colossians 2:23 (KJV) For if ye live after the flesh, ye shall die: but if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live. Romans 8:13 (KJV) Mitchell did say that God “can do anything he desires to do in the context of his will.” That’s true, and it should have governed the whole sermon. A pastor should also use great care before calling most of his church to a seven-day water fast, since any large congregation holds many people with medical reasons that make such a fast unwise.

title: Philip Anthony Mitchell
text: Signs, Tongues, and Healing Reports Mitchell is a continuationist, meaning he believes the miraculous gifts continue in the church today. Preaching on Acts 2:42-47 he said, “the Holy Spirit still does signs and wonders through people,” and “We still lay hands and see healing.” In his sermon on Acts 2:1-13 he said the tongues of 1 Corinthians 14 are different from Pentecost, that “Paul tells that this is a gift for prayer,” and that it “requires a gift of interpretation.” In a sermon reported by Charisma he said, “Suddenly, He can heal a physical body.” He has also published healing reports, like the deaf girl at ACCESS, with no evidence beyond the report itself. He isn’t a classic Pentecostal. He doesn’t teach tongues as the required sign of Spirit baptism, and he ties Spirit baptism to conversion. He has also spoken tenderly of a church member who died, saying, “although she was not physically healed in this life, she is completely healed right now.” That’s the right comfort for grieving saints, and it shows he doesn’t teach that God always heals. Reformed churches confess that God still heals, and that he answers the prayers of his people for the sick. James 5 calls the elders to pray over the sick, and believers should do so with faith. What the Confession denies is that the revealing gifts and sign gifts that marked the apostolic age go on as an ordinary part of church life. Healing claims announced from a pulpit or on social media, with no names and no proof, also put the honor of Christ at risk. When such reports prove false, unbelievers mock, and believers who were not healed grow confused about God. A man isn’t a false teacher simply because he is a continuationist. Many godly brothers hold that view. But for a Reformed believer this is a real line, and in Mitchell’s case it feeds the larger problem described under claims of direct words from God .

title: Philip Anthony Mitchell
text: Assurance and Perseverance Mitchell affirms election, yet he speaks of the believer’s final salvation as hanging on the believer. In “Blessed in Christ,” preached in October 2026 from Ephesians 1, he said, “the one who adopted you will bring you all the way into the kingdom so long as you stay in his will.” A clip that circulated in early 2025 carries his line, “Too many of you think once saved always saved.” In “Woe to You” he warned that “people who used to be on fire are no longer on fire.” His burden is partly right. Many Americans presume they are saved because they once prayed a prayer, and Scripture warns them. The foolish virgins thought they were ready. The Reformed faith has never taught that a man may live in open rebellion and rest on a past decision. But the Reformed faith also doesn’t hang final salvation on the believer’s staying power. They whom God hath accepted in his Beloved, effectually called and sanctified by his Spirit, can neither totally nor finally fall away from the state of grace; but shall certainly persevere therein to the end, and be eternally saved. Westminster Confession of Faith 17.1 And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father’s hand. John 10:28-29 (KJV) Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ: Philippians 1:6 (KJV) The sinner who truly believes will persevere, and he perseveres because God keeps him. Warnings are one of the means God uses to keep him, so a faithful preacher holds the warning and the promise together. Mitchell gives the warning loudly and the promise faintly. A doubting saint who hears “so long as you stay in his will” will look inward at his own record and find no rest there. The Reformed answer turns his eyes to Christ, who loses none of those the Father gave him. This research found no evidence that Mitchell teaches sinless perfection or that a single sin undoes salvation. His view is best described as unsettled and leaning toward conditional security. Believers who struggle with assurance should be especially careful here, and may find help in Will God Keep Me to the End?

title: Philip Anthony Mitchell
text: Handling the Text Mitchell calls himself an expository preacher, and he does preach through whole books of the Bible. That’s a good practice. But at times his application goes beyond what the text says. In “Be a Witness,” preached in April 2026, he said Jesus told the parable of the ten virgins to show that at his return “he would find half of his people ready for his return and another half of his people who was not ready for his return.” This is a good place to think about what in Scripture is meant literally and what is meant as a figure. A parable is a true lesson told through a story. Its details serve the main point, and they aren’t always meant to be read as hard facts. Five wise and five foolish sets the two kinds side by side. It isn’t a count of how many professing Christians will be ready on the last day. Notice also that both groups slept. While the bridegroom tarried, they all slumbered and slept. Matthew 25:5 (KJV) The wise were not wiser because they stayed awake. They were wiser because they had oil. In his earlier sermon on this parable, “A Cry for Readiness,” Mitchell taught it better. He noted that “all of the women fell asleep” and said the foolish “represent every man and woman who thinks they are Christians, but they are really not.” That’s sound. The later line about “half of his people” shows a habit of loose application that careful hearers need to watch for, and that risk grows for any preacher who goes into the pulpit without notes.

title: Philip Anthony Mitchell
text: Money, Tickets, and Answering Critics In 2026 Mitchell and Tim Timberlake, senior pastor of Celebration Church in Jacksonville, Florida, took their Street Preachers podcast on an eight-city tour. General admission ran about $60 to $70. A $200 VIP ticket added a meet-and-greet with the hosts, a free book, and merchandise discounts. Every stop sold out. When Christians objected, Mitchell answered from the pulpit. He said the tour was paid for from his own pocket and not by his church, that venues and security cost money, and that “We’re not doing this for a bag.” He also called his critics a “brood of vipers,” the words John the Baptist used for the Pharisees, and he pointed to a child he said was healed at one of the events. On The Breakfast Club he said he takes no offering at Sunday services and that he is “not a grifter.” This research found no evidence that Mitchell preaches a prosperity gospel, and ACCESS itself was free. Scripture also allows those who preach to be paid for their labor. Even so hath the Lord ordained that they which preach the gospel should live of the gospel. 1 Corinthians 9:14 (KJV) Yet selling time with a preacher is a different thing from covering the cost of a room. Paul set himself apart from those who made a trade of the Word. For we are not as many, which corrupt the word of God: but as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God speak we in Christ. 2 Corinthians 2:17 (KJV) Premier Christianity noted that Mitchell’s long rebuttal never addressed the VIP ticket, which drew the strongest objection. Branding fellow believers who raise a concern as a “brood of vipers” also isn’t the gentle answer a shepherd owes. When a celebrated preacher answers criticism by naming his critics Pharisees, he teaches a great many young believers that any question about their preacher is an attack from the devil. Feed the flock of God which is among you, taking the oversight thereof, not by constraint, but willingly; not for filthy lucre, but of a ready mind; neither as being lords over God’s heritage, but being ensamples to the flock. 1 Peter 5:2-3 (KJV) By comparison, his giving appeals to his own church have been measured. In early 2025 he asked for a special offering toward a five million dollar building over thirty-six months. He used the language of sowing, but he named no amount and promised no harvest, and he said, “if this makes you feel uncomfortable, then don’t do it.” That’s to his credit.

title: Philip Anthony Mitchell
text: Training, Associations, and Influences A man’s teachers don’t settle his doctrine, but they do shape the way he thinks. Mitchell’s formal Bible training came from Valor Christian College, founded by Rod Parsley at World Harvest Church in Columbus, Ohio. He graduated as valedictorian in 2010, and in a sermon on honor he said that to throw the Bible his school gave him on the floor would “dishonor Pastor Parsley.” Parsley’s ministry is a classic Pentecostal seed-faith ministry. A current appeal on his website promises “seven powerful blessings of atonement for you when you bring an offering,” including “FINANCIAL overflow” and “A DOUBLE portion from the Lord.” Critics have also tied Parsley to dominionist politics. Mitchell has not taken up Parsley’s money teaching, and he openly rejects it. Even so, the “double anointing” prayer in Israel, the talk of portals and demands, the fasting promises, and the pulpit healing reports all fit the world in which he was trained. This research found no public statement in which Mitchell distances himself from that school or its founder. His other ties are mixed. In one sermon he said, “Thank God for Jakes,” speaking of T.D. Jakes, a preacher long tied to Oneness Pentecostalism and prosperity teaching, and he gave no word of caution. He co-hosts with Tim Timberlake, appears on TBN, and is promoted by Charisma magazine. On the other side, he has been welcomed on Josh Howerton’s program, the author Jackie Hill Perry and her husband Preston Perry attend 2819, and the church’s worship team has partnered with Reach Records. No evidence was found that Mitchell belongs to the New Apostolic Reformation or claims the office of apostle. He is best described as a conservative charismatic evangelical, trained in Pentecostal circles, who has moved toward a sharper doctrine of sin and grace while keeping many charismatic habits of speech and practice.

title: Philip Anthony Mitchell
text: The Church and Its Government 2819 Church is nondenominational. Its written statement confesses the Trinity, the full deity and full humanity of Christ, the inspiration and inerrancy of Scripture, and salvation by grace through faith. It practices believer’s baptism and a memorial Lord’s Supper with bread and grape juice. Those last two points differ from Presbyterian conviction, though many faithful Baptists share them. Its government is much less clear. Mitchell refers to “the elders,” and the church names him and his wife Lena as its leaders, but it publishes no list of elders, no account of how leaders are chosen or held accountable, and no plan of church discipline. In a 2025 sermon he told visitors there is no membership requirement at 2819. A church of thousands, with tens of thousands more “Digital Disciples” watching online, can’t be shepherded the way Hebrews 13:17 describes unless the shepherds know the sheep and the sheep belong to a flock. A livestream can’t do that work.

title: Philip Anthony Mitchell
section: Worship and the Danger of Idolizing a Preacher
text: Worship and the Danger of Idolizing a Preacher The Lord’s Day gathering at 2819 Church is built like a concert. Reporters have described a countdown clock, loud music and percussion, strobe lights, and a smoke machine. Volunteers pray over each seat, greeters dance, and the worship team moves from a fast song into a slow one while the room lifts its hands. People line up before dawn to get in, and some travel hundreds of miles each Sunday. ACCESS carried the same pattern into the arenas, with a produced program and tens of thousands gathered around one preacher. What God requires in worship Reformed churches hold what is called the regulative principle of worship. God alone decides how he is to be worshipped, and the church may add nothing he has not commanded. But the acceptable way of worshipping the true God is instituted by himself, and so limited by his own revealed will, that he may not be worshipped according to the imaginations and devices of men, or the suggestions of Satan, under any visible representation, or any other way not prescribed in the holy Scripture. Westminster Confession of Faith 21.1 Smoke, strobes, and countdown clocks are devices of men. They exist to shape the mood of a room, and they work on the feelings whether the preacher intends it or not. When a gathering is built that way, it becomes very hard for anyone in the room to tell the work of the Spirit from the work of the lighting. God has given his church plain means for worship in the reading and preaching of the Word, prayer, the singing of praise, and the sacraments. Those means need no help from a production team. Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear: for our God is a consuming fire. Hebrews 12:28-29 (KJV) Feelings aren’t the enemy. David danced before the Lord, and the Psalms are full of tears and shouts. But holy affection rises out of truth understood. When a room is engineered to stir the feelings first, people learn to measure God’s presence by what they feel, and they go looking for the next service or the next stadium that can make them feel it again. Signs of a culture built around one man Concern about idolizing Mitchell has been raised in public and more than once. Reporters note the enthusiastic reaction whenever he takes the stage, and one observer reported that some members have begun dressing like him. VIP tickets that included a meet-and-greet with him sold for $200, and every stop on the Street Preachers tour sold out. In 2025 a woman interrupted a service to call the church to repent of idolizing its pastor, and security removed her. In August 2026 a visiting minister said he was removed after raising the same concern. The matter has come up often enough that Mitchell addressed it on The Breakfast Club , saying “there is a difference between idolization and admiration.” Mitchell says the right things about it. He has told his church, “He’s just a man. Come feel God’s presence. It’s much better,” and he has urged them to thank God for growth “and not idolize a preacher.” He should be taken at his word that he wants no worship for himself. But his platform pulls against his warnings. He sells paid time with himself on tour. He builds stadium events around his own voice. He tells his church, “If you don’t like the vessel, pray for the vessel, especially if God sent the vessel.” His whole ministry rests on a story of a personal charge from God in Israel. Every one of those things lifts the man, and none of them is required by his calling. A preacher who means his warnings will take down the platforms that feed the problem. John the Baptist showed the right spirit. He must increase, but I must decrease. John 3:30 (KJV) Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos, but ministers by whom ye believed, even as the Lord gave to every man? I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase. So then neither is he that planteth any thing, neither he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase. 1 Corinthians 3:5-7 (KJV) Why this makes him a particular danger Movements like Bethel Church in Redding, California, are easy for conservative believers to spot. Mitchell is much harder to spot. He sounds like a sound evangelical. He preaches sin and repentance and grace, and he draws young believers who would never go near Bethel. So his errors reach ears that are otherwise on guard. His growth has been sudden and enormous. He relaunched with 183 people in January 2023. He now draws about 6,000 a week in person and tens of thousands online, and in the space of a year he filled State Farm Arena and then AT&T Stadium. If he keeps teaching the errors documented in this report at that scale, inside a culture of spectacle that lifts the preacher, he will do as much harm as Bethel has done. He will do it through a door that conservative churches have left open.

title: Philip Anthony Mitchell
section: What This Report Does Not Charge
text: What This Report Does Not Charge Some charges against Mitchell pass from video to video without proof. Fairness means saying plainly which ones the record does not support, so that no one repeats them. He is not shown to belong to the New Apostolic Reformation. No evidence was found that he is part of it or claims the office of apostle. He does not preach a money-for-blessing gospel. He rejects the prosperity gospel by name, teaches that the tithe does not bind the New Testament believer, and promised no harvest when he asked his church to give. He does not teach that God always heals. He has comforted grieving families with the hope that a saint who died unhealed is “completely healed right now.”

title: Philip Anthony Mitchell
text: Summary of Findings The weight given to each finding follows the Westminster Standards. A grave finding touches the foundation of the faith. A serious finding departs from clear Reformed teaching in a way that harms hearers. A caution marks a weakness believers should watch for. Gospel of grace. Sound Denies works salvation and preaches Christ’s righteousness counted to the believer. Person of Christ. Grave Taught that the Son emptied himself “of some of his divine nature.” No correction found. Revelation. Serious Regular claims of direct words and charges from God, outside Scripture. Prayer. Serious Called ACCESS “a portal from earth to heaven” and spoke of putting “a demand” on God. Fasting. Serious Said fasting can “move God” and promised that bodies would be healed. Spiritual gifts. Caution Trained under Rod Parsley, commends T.D. Jakes. No tie to the New Apostolic Reformation found. Church order. Caution No published eldership, accountability, or membership. Worship. title: Philip Anthony Mitchell
text: Counsel for the Saints Should Christians listen to Philip Anthony Mitchell? The answer of this report is no, not as a teacher to sit under. A believer may hear a clip and find something true in it, and truth is still truth when it comes from a man with errors. But a teacher is someone we trust to feed us week after week. Mitchell’s errors reach the person of Christ, the sufficiency of Scripture, and the nature of prayer itself, and those are not side issues. My brethren, be not many masters, knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation. James 3:1 (KJV) Where should saints be most careful with him? Test anything he says about who Jesus is against the Creed and the Confession, beginning with the “Stay Awake” sermon. When he says God told him something, ask where God said it in his Word. Language about portals, atmospheres, and demands should send you back to Hebrews 10, where Christ alone is our way to the Father. Promises of healing or breakthrough tied to fasting or to a gathering need a promise from God behind them, and he doesn’t supply one. And when he warns about false assurance, take the warning to heart, but rest your soul on the promise that Christ keeps his own. How should saints speak of him? With truth and with charity. Quote his own words when naming his errors. Don’t call him a wolf or a deceiver without proof of his motives, and don’t repeat charges the record doesn’t support. And pray for him. He has shown that he can humble himself and correct a public mistake. Christians should pray that he does the same about the person of Christ and the authority of Scripture. For regular feeding, point believers first to the faithful preaching of their own church, where elders know their names and watch over their souls. For further help, point them to men whose doctrine has stood the test of time, such as R.C. Sproul, Sinclair Ferguson, John MacArthur, Voddie Baucham, and Paul Washer, and behind them to J.C. Ryle, Charles Spurgeon, and the Puritans. Mitchell named his new book after the letter of Jude. The saints would do well to take that verse seriously. Beloved, when I gave all diligence to write unto you of the common salvation, it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints. Jude 3 (KJV) Contending for the faith begins with the faith about Christ himself. That’s where Mitchell most needs correction, and it’s where the church must stand most firmly.

title: About
text: About Gentle King What This Is Gentle King is a layman’s work. It is a place to set out the gospel and sound doctrine where anyone can reach them without paying for them. Two tools are made here and given away. Sojourner is a Bible study app for your phone, tablet, or computer, and Mortify is an app for the daily fight against sin. They serve the work. They are not the heart of it. The name comes from the King himself. He rode into Jerusalem on a borrowed donkey. Isaiah said of him that he will not break a bruised reed or quench the smoking flax. He calls tired people to come to him, and he gives them rest. Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. Matthew 11:28-29 (KJV) He is gentle, and his authority is real. Those two things are not at odds. The throne is what makes the kindness worth anything. This site is not a church, and it is no substitute for one. A website cannot preach to you, baptize you, feed you at the Lord’s Table, or watch over your soul. Christ gave those things to his church. Nothing here binds your conscience either. Scripture does that. The supreme Judge, by which all controversies of religion are to be determined, and all decrees of councils, opinions of ancient writers, doctrines of men, and private spirits, are to be examined, and in whose sentence we are to rest, can be no other but the Holy Spirit speaking in the Scripture. Westminster Confession of Faith 1.10 So read with your Bible open. If something written here does not agree with it, throw that thing out and keep the Bible.

title: About
text: Who writes this Who I Am My name is Colt. I am a husband and a father of two. I work as a custodian, and I study and write and build software in the hours around that work. I am not a pastor. I am not an elder. I hold no office and have no credentials to put in front of you. I am a layman in the Reformed Presbyterian tradition who was shown mercy he never had coming, and who wants to hand some of it on. This site is not a platform for me. I am not looking for a following. For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus’ sake. 2 Corinthians 4:5 (KJV) If anything here helps you see Christ more clearly, that is his doing. If anything here is wrong, it is mine, and I would rather know than be flattered.

title: About
text: Statement of faith What I Believe A short summary, put plainly. Not a new confession, only an honest account of the faith everything here is written from. The Scriptures The sixty-six books of the Old and New Testaments are the Word of God, breathed out by him, true in all they teach, and the only infallible rule of faith and life. All of it points to Christ. God and the Trinity One living and true God, infinite, eternal, and unchangeable in his being, wisdom, power, holiness, justice, goodness, and truth. In the one divine being there are three persons, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the same in substance, equal in power and glory. The Father is not the Son, and the Son is not the Spirit, yet there is one God and not three. Man and Sin God made man upright and in his own image. In Adam we fell. We come into the world guilty, corrupt at the root, and justly under the wrath of God. Sin is no weakness to manage. It earns death. The Person of Christ The eternal Son of God took a true human nature into union with his divine person and will never lay it down. Two natures, one person, forever. He is the one mediator between God and men. The Work of Christ He kept the law we broke. He died in the place of his people, bearing the wrath our sins deserved. He rose bodily, ascended, and reigns now at the Father’s right hand, praying for all the Father gave him. Not one will be lost. Salvation By grace alone, through faith alone, in Christ alone. God justifies the ungodly by crediting to them the perfect righteousness of Christ, which faith simply receives. Good works follow that verdict gladly. They never purchase it. And Christ is held out freely to everyone who hears, so that no one who comes to him is turned away. The Holy Spirit He convicts of sin, gives new birth to a dead heart, unites the sinner to Christ, works faith and repentance, and finishes what he starts. A dead man does not believe and then come alive. The Spirit gives life first, and faith is what that new life does. The Church and the Sacraments Christ has one church, gathered under his Word, led by officers he appointed, fed by the ordinary means of grace, which are the Word, the sacraments, and prayer. Baptism and the Lord’s Supper are signs and seals of the covenant of grace, not empty ceremony. The Christian Life The law is no ladder to climb for life. It is the rule a freed son gladly walks by. The believer puts sin to death by the Spirit and grows slowly and really. Sanctification always follows justification and never grounds it. Last Things Jesus Christ will return bodily, visibly, and in glory. The dead will be raised. He will judge the living and the dead, send the impenitent into everlasting punishment, and make all things new. Those are certainties. On the millennium I am amillennial. I hold it with an open hand toward brothers who read it otherwise, since faithful Reformed men land in different places there. For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast. Ephesians 2:8-9 (KJV) The fuller statement is not mine. This site holds the Westminster Confession of Faith, with the Larger and Shorter Catechisms, as its doctrinal standard. I receive them as my own church receives them, as a faithful summary of what the Bible teaches. Everything here is written to stand within them. This site is my own work, not my church’s, and its elders do not answer for it. The Standards are quoted here from the text of 1647. Read the Confession in full at The Westminster Standard , and see the doctrine page for more.

God does not want his children living on guesses. John wrote his first letter to believers so that they would know they have eternal life (1 John 5:13). 4 min read When the Same Sin Keeps Coming Back Few things shake a Christian like meeting the same sin again, years after he first wept over it. Your fear draws one conclusion from that. God has drawn another, and he has written it down. 5 min read The Unpardonable Sin and Falling Away Some fears come back at night, when the house is quiet and there is nothing to do but think. Each of these has an answer that will not give way under you. 5 min read When God Feels Far There are seasons when prayer feels like talking to the ceiling and the Bible is only ink. They do not mean that God has gone. 4 min read Doubts and Unwanted Thoughts Some believers are afraid it is not true, and the question will not leave them alone. title: Why Doctrine Matters
text: Why sound teaching belongs to the Christian life.

title: Why Doctrine Matters
section: Why Doctrine Is Not the Enemy of Devotion
text: Why Doctrine Is Not the Enemy of Devotion Start Here Doctrine is simply what you believe about God. You already have some. The only real question is whether it is true. People sometimes say they want Jesus and not doctrine. But the moment you say the name Jesus you have said something doctrinal. You have said he is real. You have said something about who he is and what he has done. The man who says God is love is teaching doctrine. So is the man who says God would never send anyone to hell. Nobody stands outside of doctrine. We only stand inside good doctrine or bad. There is a real danger here, and it should be named. A person can know the terms and never know the Lord. He can argue well and pray little. That is a hard and pitiful thing, and Scripture warns about it. But the cure for cold knowledge is not less knowledge. It is knowledge that reaches the heart. You cannot love a God you have refused to learn anything about. You cannot trust a Savior whose work you have never understood. The doctrines on this page are not a cage around Christ. They are windows. Each one lets more light in on his face. If ye continue in my word, then are ye my disciples indeed; And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free. John 8:31-32 (KJV) So read slowly. Look up what is cited. Ask God to show you himself in it.

title: The Bible
text: Why Scripture is our final rule of faith and life.

title: The Bible
text: The Word of God Sola Scriptura Everything else on this page rests here. If God has not spoken, we have nothing to say. God has spoken, and his speech has been written down. The old word for it is inspiration. The Bible did not float down from heaven. Men wrote it, in their own words and settings and styles, and the Holy Spirit carried them along so that what they wrote is what God says. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works. 2 Timothy 3:16-17 (KJV) Because God breathed it out, and because God does not lie, the Bible is true in all that it affirms. Inerrancy is not a claim that every copy and every translation is perfect. It is a claim about what God gave. Because God gave it for this purpose, it is enough. Sufficiency means you do not need a new revelation in order to be saved and to live before God. You do not need a private word or a hidden tradition either. The whole counsel of God needed for salvation, faith and life is either expressly set down in Scripture or follows from it by good and necessary consequence, as the Confession says in WCF 1.6. And because God meant to be understood, the Bible is clear where it matters most. Not every verse is equally easy. Peter said as much about Paul. But the things you must know to be saved are set out clearly enough that an unlearned reader, using the ordinary means, can understand them. WCF 1.7 says so, and it is why a working man with a Bible and a lunch break can feed on the Word of God. What then about the confessions and catechisms this site holds? They are subordinate standards. They are a faithful summary of what Scripture teaches, tested by the church across centuries, and they sit under the Bible and never beside it. The supreme Judge, by which all controversies of religion are to be determined, and all decrees of councils, opinions of ancient writers, doctrines of men, and private spirits, are to be examined, and in whose sentence we are to rest, can be no other but the Holy Spirit speaking in the Scripture. Westminster Confession of Faith 1.10

title: God and the Trinity
text: The one living God, Father, Son, and Holy Ghost.

title: God and the Trinity
text: God, and God as Trinity Theology Proper Before there was a world to save, there was God. He was not lonely. He was not waiting. He was full. God is spirit, infinite, eternal and unchangeable in his being, wisdom, power, holiness, justice, goodness and truth. He did not come from anywhere. He does not grow or shrink or improve. He is not one part of the universe, and the universe is not one part of him. He made it out of nothing and upholds it every second by the word of his power. His attributes are not pieces bolted together. God is not partly holy and partly loving. Everything in God is God. His love is holy love. His justice is good justice. His mercy never embarrasses his righteousness. How God can be just and still justify the ungodly is exactly the question the cross answers. Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God is one Lord : Deuteronomy 6:4 (KJV) This one God exists as three persons. Not three gods. Not one person wearing three masks. The Father is God, the Son is God, the Holy Spirit is God, and there is one God. The Father is not the Son, the Son is not the Spirit, and the Spirit is not the Father. Each person is fully and equally God, undivided in essence, distinct in person. The Confession puts the distinction carefully in WCF 2.3. The Father is of none, the Son is eternally begotten of the Father, and the Holy Spirit eternally proceeds from the Father and the Son. None of it is a matter of one person coming after another in time or ranking below another in being. There are three persons in the Godhead; the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost; and these three are one God, the same in substance, equal in power and glory. Westminster Shorter Catechism Q&A 6 This is not a riddle invented by councils. It is what the Bible forces on anyone who reads it whole. Jesus sends his people to baptize in one name that belongs to Father, Son and Holy Spirit. Salvation itself is Trinitarian. The Father chooses, the Son redeems, the Spirit applies. If you have been saved, all three persons have been at work on you. Guard your words here. Every homespun illustration of the Trinity, water and ice and steam, a man who is father and son and husband, ends up teaching an old heresy. It is better to say less and say it carefully.

title: The Five Solas
text: Salvation by grace alone through faith alone in Christ alone.

title: The Five Solas
text: Alone Means Alone The Five Solas The Reformation did not recover five slogans. It recovered one gospel, and these are the five hinges it turns on. Sola Scriptura, Scripture alone Scripture is the only infallible rule for faith and life. Tradition can be useful and pastors can be gifted, but only the Bible binds the conscience. Everything else is weighed and either received or set aside. Sola Gratia, grace alone Salvation begins in God, not in you. You did not contribute the deciding factor. Grace is not God meeting you halfway once you make the first move. Grace is God coming all the way down to a dead man and giving him life. Sola Fide, faith alone You are justified by faith, apart from works of the law. Faith is not a good deed that earns a reward. It reaches out and takes. Even the faith is a gift, which is why no one will boast in heaven. Solus Christus, Christ alone There is one mediator between God and men. No saint, no priest, no sacrament, no sincerity of yours stands in that place. Christ obeyed where Adam failed and bore the wrath his people owed. He rose, ascended, and prays for his people now. Soli Deo Gloria, to God alone be glory If salvation is by grace, through faith, in Christ, according to Scripture, then the credit has only one address. This is not God being vain. It is God being honest about who did the saving. For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast. Ephesians 2:8-9 (KJV) At the center of all five sits justification. God declares the guilty righteous, not by making them righteous first, but by pardoning their sins and counting Christ’s righteousness as theirs. Those whom God effectually calleth, He also freely justifieth: not by infusing righteousness into them, but by pardoning their sins, and by accounting and accepting their persons as righteous; not for any thing wrought in them, or done by them, but for Christ’s sake alone. Westminster Confession of Faith 11.1 Sanctification follows that verdict. It never props it up. You obey because you are accepted, never in order to become accepted. The gospel page works out the imputed righteousness of Christ at length.

title: The Doctrines of Grace
text: How God brings sinners to Christ and keeps them.

title: The Doctrines of Grace
text: How God Saves Sinners The Doctrines of Grace These five points were never meant to be the whole of the faith. They are an answer to a specific question. When God saves a sinner, who does the saving? Read them as one sentence about one God working one salvation. Taken apart they can sound cold. Taken together they are a deep comfort, because they mean your salvation does not finally rest on how tightly you hold on. Total Depravity Also called total inability Sin has touched every part of us, mind and will and affections, so that no one seeks God on his own. The word total is about extent, not degree. No part of us is clean enough to save the rest. Paul lays this out in Romans 3, and Ephesians 2 calls us dead in trespasses. Unconditional Election Ephesians 1:4-5 Before the foundation of the world God set his love on a people in Christ. The choice was not made because he looked down the corridors of time and saw who would choose him. It rested on the good pleasure of his will. Paul defends it at length in Romans 9, including the objections it raises. Particular Redemption Commonly called limited atonement Christ did not die to make salvation merely possible. He died to actually save particular people, and he will not lose them. His death is of infinite worth, and Christ is freely offered in the gospel to every sinner who hears, but its saving design and effect are for his sheep. Effectual Calling Sometimes called irresistible grace Alongside the outward call of the gospel to all, the Spirit gives an inward call that raises the dead. Ezekiel 36 promised it, and the new birth is where God makes good on the promise. New life comes first, and then the sinner comes willingly, because he has been made willing. Perseverance of the Saints Kept by the power of God Those truly united to Christ will be kept to the end. They may fall badly and grieve the Spirit, but they will be brought back. This is not a promise that a prayer you once prayed guarantees heaven. It is a promise that what God began in you he will bring to completion, as Philippians 1:6 says. I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep. John 10:11 (KJV) He does not say he makes a sheepfold available. He lays down his life for the sheep, and he gets them. All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out. John 6:37 (KJV) Both halves of that verse are yours to hold. The first half tells you election works. The second half tells you the door is open, right now, to you. If you are worried about whether you are chosen, stop looking inward and come to Christ. Nobody who comes is turned away. For a fuller answer to the views these points were written against, see How to Answer Arminianism and Pelagianism .

title: Covenant Theology
text: One covenant of grace across the Old and New Testaments.

title: Covenant Theology
text: One Story, Two Testaments Covenant Theology God has always dealt with his people by covenant. Learn the covenants and the Bible stops feeling like a pile of disconnected stories. Before creation, in eternity, the persons of the Trinity agreed on redemption. The Father gave a people to the Son, the Son agreed to obey and suffer for them, and the Spirit agreed to apply that work to them. Reformed writers call this the covenant of redemption. It is the reason Jesus speaks so often about those the Father has given him. In the garden God dealt with Adam in a covenant of works. Perfect obedience, and life. Disobedience, and death. Adam stood there not only for himself but for all who would come from him. He failed, and the ruin spread to every one of us. God did not walk away. He made a second covenant, the covenant of grace, and he made it at cost to himself. Man by his fall having made himself incapable of life by that covenant, the Lord was pleased to make a second, commonly called the covenant of grace; wherein He freely offereth unto sinners life and salvation by Jesus Christ; requiring of them faith in Him, that they may be saved, and promising to give unto all those that are ordained unto eternal life His Holy Spirit, to make them willing, and able to believe. Westminster Confession of Faith 7.3 Here is the part that changes your reading. There are not two ways of salvation in the Bible, law for the old and grace for the new. There is one covenant of grace administered in two ways. Under the old administration it came through promise, sacrifice, priesthood and shadow. Under the new it comes with the substance itself, Christ crucified and risen, preached to the nations. Abraham was justified by faith exactly as you are. The difference is that he looked forward and you look back. And if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise. Galatians 3:29 (KJV) So when you open Leviticus, you are not reading a foreign religion. You are watching God teach his people, in blood and smoke and careful ritual, what sin costs and what a substitute is for. When you read the prophets, you are hearing a covenant Lord pleading with a covenant people. And when you reach the Supper, you hear Jesus say the cup is the new covenant in his blood, and the whole Old Testament leans forward into that sentence.

title: Law and Gospel
text: What God commands and what he gives in Christ.

title: Law and Gospel
text: Two Words From One God Law and Gospel The law tells you what God requires. The gospel tells you what God has done. Confuse them and you will lose both. The law is holy, and it is not the problem. We are. God’s law puts his own character into commandments, and it does three kinds of work. The law restrains. Even among people who hate God, the law written on the conscience and echoed in a nation’s laws holds back some of the evil that would otherwise swallow us. It shows you what you are. Held up to the commandments, you stop guessing about yourself. The law was never given as a ladder. It is a mirror, and it drives the honest sinner to Christ. For the believer, it guides. Already justified and safe, he takes the law as the rule of a grateful life. This is the third use, and Reformed Christians have always insisted on it. Two errors wait on either side of this teaching, and both are deadly. Legalism takes the law and makes it the ground of acceptance. It says God will love you if you clean yourself up. It turns obedience into a payment and Christ into an assistant. The legalist is either crushed or proud, and often both in the same week. Antinomianism takes grace and uses it as permission. It says that since works do not justify, obedience does not matter. Paul had already heard that argument and he did not treat it gently. What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound? God forbid. How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer therein? Romans 6:1-2 (KJV) The Confession says in WCF 19.6 and 19.7 that the believer is free from the law as a covenant of works and is still bound to it as a rule of life, and that these uses of the law are not contrary to the grace of the gospel but sweetly comply with it. The commandments no longer threaten a justified man with the curse. They show him what love looks like in the concrete. You keep the law because you are loved, never to become loved.

title: The Church and Worship
text: The church, worship, and the ordinary means of grace.

title: The Church and Worship
text: Where Christ Feeds His People The Church Christ did not save you and leave you on your own. He put you in a body, and he set a table in it. The church is not a building and it is not an audience. It is the people Christ has bought, gathered under his rule, united to him and to each other. He has appointed unglamorous means by which he gives his grace, and they have not changed. The outward and ordinary means whereby Christ communicateth to us the benefits of redemption are his ordinances, especially the word, sacraments, and prayer; all which are made effectual to the elect for salvation. Westminster Shorter Catechism Q&A 88 The preached word comes first. Not a talk about the Bible, but the Bible opened, explained and pressed home, with Christ held out in it. God has been pleased to save and to strengthen through this plain thing week after week. Baptism is a sign and seal of the covenant of grace, marking the washing away of sin, union with Christ in his death and resurrection, and belonging to God’s people. The Westminster Standards hold that it belongs to believers and to their children, as the covenant sign always has. The water does not save. It signifies and seals what God does. The Lord’s Supper is not a fresh sacrifice, and it is not a bare memory either. Christ is really present, not bodily but spiritually, and he is received by faith as his people eat and drink. It is a meal for those who trust him and grieve their sin, not a reward for those who have arrived. And they continued stedfastly in the apostles’ doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers. Acts 2:42 (KJV) This is why membership matters. To join a church is to say you will be known, taught, corrected and cared for by particular people, and to place yourself under elders who will answer to God for your soul. Discipline belongs to that same care. It is not punishment for its own sake. It aims at repentance and restoration, and where the sin is private, it begins quietly and privately. On worship, the Reformed hold what is called the regulative principle. God himself determines how he is to be worshiped, and we come with what he has commanded rather than with what we have invented, as WCF 21.1 states. In practice that means Scripture read and preached, prayer, singing, the sacraments and the offering of ourselves. This site holds it as the Reformed Presbyterian churches do, with the Psalms sung in worship without instruments. Other Presbyterians hold the same principle and apply it differently, and those disagreements are worth having honestly and without contempt. How God Wants to Be Worshiped sets it out plainly.

title: The End Times
text: Christ’s return, the resurrection, and the judgment.

title: The End Times
section: How It Ends, and What Is Settled
text: How It Ends, and What Is Settled Eschatology Start with what every Reformed believer confesses. It is more than most people expect, and it is enough to live and die on. Christ is reigning now, seated at the right hand of the Father, with all authority in heaven and on earth. He will return bodily, visibly, personally. The dead will be raised bodily, the righteous and the wicked alike. There will be a final judgment, real and just, and the wicked will be punished forever. Those in Christ will be acquitted openly and welcomed. Then come the new heavens and the new earth, where righteousness dwells and God himself lives with his people. And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away. Revelation 21:4 (KJV) From here on, faithful men differ. The question is how the thousand years of Revelation 20 relates to the present age and to Christ’s return. Three historic answers have been held by confessional Reformed Christians. Amillennialism Held widely in Reformed churches The thousand years is the whole present age between Christ’s first and second comings. Satan is bound from deceiving the nations so the gospel can go out, the souls of the departed reign with Christ now, and the kingdom advances through the Word while the world stays a mix of wheat and weeds. Christ returns once, and judgment and the new creation follow immediately. Postmillennialism Held by many Puritans and by Edwards The same gospel that saves one sinner will, in God’s time, bring an age of widespread blessing, when the nations are discipled in great numbers and Christ’s rule is honored broadly on earth before he returns. That age is the fruit of ordinary preaching and the Spirit’s power, not a separate dispensation. Christ returns at the close of it to judge and to make all things new. Historic Premillennialism An old view, distinct from dispensationalism Christ returns first, and a real reign on earth follows his coming. The church passes through tribulation and is not removed from it. This view is ancient, and it is not built on a separation between Israel and the church. The man who writes this site is amillennial, and he holds the first view above. He holds it as his own reading of Scripture and not as a test of fellowship. These are matters where brothers who confess the same Christ and the same Confession have differed in peace for centuries, and they should keep differing in peace. Two cautions, though. Do not treat dispensational premillennialism, with its sharp split between Israel and the church and its secret rapture, as the Reformed position. It is not, and it came late. And do not let curiosity about the end replace readiness for it. The last things were given to make you holy and to comfort you while you wait.

title: The Westminster Standards
text: Where to begin with the Westminster Standards.

title: The Westminster Standards
section: The Standards, and the Savior in Them
text: The Standards, and the Savior in Them Where to Go Next None of this was worked out in a hurry, and you do not have to work it out alone. The Westminster Confession of Faith, the Shorter Catechism and the Larger Catechism are among the clearest short summaries of the faith written in English. The Shorter Catechism is the place to begin. It is short and memorable, and it answers the first question a human being ought to ask. Read the full text at The Westminster Standard , where the Confession is posted with its proof texts. Take it slowly. One question a day with a Bible open beside it will do more for you in a year than a stack of books read fast. The Standards were written for the church, and no website can take the church’s place. Find a faithful local church under the ordinary means of grace, join it, and sit under the Word. If the gospel itself is still unclear to you, go to the gospel page first, because that is the doctrine everything else serves. And remember who all of this is about. The King who ordained the covenant before the world was, and who will judge the living and the dead, says this to you. Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. Matthew 11:28-29 (KJV) Learn the doctrine so you can see more of him, and then go to him. If something here raised a question you cannot settle, you are welcome to write and ask .
